# Caddy CA distributor (`caddy_ca_v1`)

HTTP bundle of Caddy `tls internal` root CAs for **private-IP** marketplace
deployments. Peer VMs (n8n, LM Studio, Open WebUI, Hermes, …) each mint their
own local CA; clients that verify TLS then fail with unknown CA.

This service does not replace those CAs. It **collects** them from
`http://<peer>/ca.crt` (exported on port 80 by Caddy-fronted services) and
serves one PEM bundle plus a JSON catalog.

## Pairing

1. Launch Caddy-fronted peers first (or in parallel — collection retries).
2. Launch `caddy_ca_v1` with their IPs (or CA URLs):

```bash
python -m cloudinit_manager caddy_ca_v1 \
  -v ca_peers=10.0.0.5,10.0.0.6,http://10.0.0.7/ca.crt
```

3. Point HTTPS clients at the bundle:

```bash
python -m cloudinit_manager n8n_v3 \
  -v ca_url=http://<caddy-ca-ip>/ca.crt

python -m cloudinit_manager openwebui_v1 \
  -v openai_base_url=https://<llmstudio-ip>.nip.io/v1 \
  -v openai_api_key=<token> \
  -v ca_url=http://<caddy-ca-ip>/ca.crt
```

`ca_url` may be a bare IP (`10.0.0.5` → `http://10.0.0.5/ca.crt`) when talking
to a single peer's exporter instead of this aggregator.

Guided Multipass demo (LM Studio + n8n runner + this distributor + n8n):
[`examples/multipass-n8n-runner-llmstudio-ca.sh`](../../examples/multipass-n8n-runner-llmstudio-ca.sh).

## Variables

| Variable | Purpose | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `ca_peers` | Comma-separated IPs / hosts / `http(s)://…/ca.crt` | empty |
| `ca_refresh_seconds` | Collector refresh interval | `60` (clamped 15–3600) |

Empty `ca_peers` still boots: `/healthz` and `/cas.json` work; `/ca.crt` appears
once at least one peer PEM is collected.

## Endpoints

| Path | Role |
|---|---|
| `GET /ca.crt` | Concatenated PEM bundle |
| `GET /cas.json` | Catalog (`source`, `ok`, `fingerprint_sha256`) |
| `GET /healthz` | Liveness |

Plain HTTP on **:80** on purpose — clients cannot bootstrap trust over the same
unknown Caddy CA.

## On-VM ops

```bash
sudo /opt/elemento/bin/healthcheck
sudo /opt/elemento/bin/service-info
journalctl -u caddy-ca-collect.service -f
docker compose -f /opt/caddy-ca/docker-compose.yml logs -f caddy
```

The collector is a host systemd unit (`caddy-ca-collect.service`). Re-run a
single pass with `sudo /opt/caddy-ca/collect-cas.sh --once`.

#!/bin/sh
# Fetch peer Caddy CA PEMs and publish a concatenated bundle on /ca.crt.
# Preferred: systemd caddy-ca-collect.service
# Canonical path: /opt/caddy-ca/collect-cas.sh
set -eu

ENV_FILE=/opt/caddy-ca/caddy-ca.env
WWW=/var/lib/caddy-ca/www
CAS=/var/lib/caddy-ca/cas

ONCE=0
if [ "${1:-}" = "--once" ]; then
  ONCE=1
fi

json_escape() {
  printf '%s' "$1" | sed 's/\\/\\\\/g; s/"/\\"/g'
}

is_placeholder() {
  _value=$1
  [ -z "$_value" ] && return 0
  echo "$_value" | grep -q '{' && return 0
  return 1
}

normalize_ca_url() {
  u=$1
  [ -n "$u" ] || return 1
  echo "$u" | grep -q '{' && return 1
  case "$u" in
    http://*|https://*)
      case "$u" in
        */ca.crt|*/cas.json|*.pem|*.crt) printf '%s\n' "$u" ;;
        */) printf '%sca.crt\n' "$u" ;;
        *) printf '%s/ca.crt\n' "$u" ;;
      esac
      ;;
    *) printf 'http://%s/ca.crt\n' "$u" ;;
  esac
}

fingerprint_pem() {
  printf '%s\n' "$1" | openssl x509 -noout -fingerprint -sha256 2>/dev/null \
    | sed 's/.*Fingerprint=//' | tr -d ':'
}

fetch_pem() {
  url=$1
  case "$url" in
    https://*) curl -fskS --max-time 10 "$url" ;;
    *) curl -fsS --max-time 10 "$url" ;;
  esac
}

publish_bundle() {
  updated=$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)
  json="${WWW}/cas.json"
  bundle_tmp="${WWW}/ca.crt.tmp"
  : > "$bundle_tmp"

  {
    printf '{\n  "api_version": "elemento.ca_bundle/v1",\n'
    printf '  "updated_at": "%s",\n' "$(json_escape "$updated")"
    printf '  "certificates": ['
  } > "$json.tmp"

  first=1
  seen_fps=""
  have_cert=0

  OLDIFS=$IFS
  IFS=','
  # shellcheck disable=SC2086
  set -- $CA_PEERS
  IFS=$OLDIFS

  for raw in "$@"; do
    raw=$(printf '%s' "$raw" | tr -d '[:space:]')
    [ -n "$raw" ] || continue
    url=$(normalize_ca_url "$raw" || true)
    [ -n "$url" ] || continue

    pem=""
    ok="false"
    fp=""
    if pem=$(fetch_pem "$url" 2>/dev/null); then
      if echo "$pem" | grep -q "BEGIN CERTIFICATE"; then
        fp=$(fingerprint_pem "$pem" || true)
        dup=0
        for seen in $seen_fps; do
          if [ -n "$fp" ] && [ "$seen" = "$fp" ]; then
            dup=1
            break
          fi
        done
        if [ "$dup" -eq 0 ]; then
          printf '%s\n' "$pem" >> "$bundle_tmp"
          echo >> "$bundle_tmp"
          have_cert=1
          if [ -n "$fp" ]; then
            seen_fps="${seen_fps} ${fp}"
          fi
        fi
        ok="true"
        safe=$(printf '%s' "$url" | tr '/:' '__')
        printf '%s\n' "$pem" > "${CAS}/${safe}.crt"
      fi
    fi

    if [ "$first" -eq 1 ]; then
      first=0
    else
      printf ',' >> "$json.tmp"
    fi
    printf '\n    {"source":"%s","ok":%s,"fingerprint_sha256":"%s"}' \
      "$(json_escape "$url")" "$ok" "$(json_escape "$fp")" >> "$json.tmp"
  done

  printf '\n  ]\n}\n' >> "$json.tmp"
  mv "$json.tmp" "$json"

  if [ "$have_cert" -eq 1 ]; then
    mv "$bundle_tmp" "${WWW}/ca.crt"
  else
    rm -f "$bundle_tmp"
    rm -f "${WWW}/ca.crt"
  fi
}

mkdir -p "$WWW" "$CAS"

while true; do
  CA_PEERS=""
  CA_REFRESH_SECONDS=60
  if [ -f "$ENV_FILE" ]; then
    # shellcheck disable=SC1090
    . "$ENV_FILE"
  fi
  if is_placeholder "${CA_PEERS:-}"; then
    CA_PEERS=""
  fi
  case "${CA_REFRESH_SECONDS:-}" in
    ''|*[!0-9]*) CA_REFRESH_SECONDS=60 ;;
  esac

  publish_bundle

  if [ "$ONCE" -eq 1 ]; then
    exit 0
  fi
  sleep "$CA_REFRESH_SECONDS"
done

#!/bin/sh
# Normalize caddy_ca_v1 env (peers, refresh interval).
set -eu

ENV_FILE=/opt/caddy-ca/caddy-ca.env

is_placeholder() {
  _value=$1
  [ -z "$_value" ] && return 0
  echo "$_value" | grep -q '{' && return 0
  return 1
}

read_env() {
  env_key=$1
  grep -E "^${env_key}=" "$ENV_FILE" 2>/dev/null | tail -1 | cut -d= -f2- || true
}

set_env() {
  env_key=$1
  env_val=$2
  if grep -q "^${env_key}=" "$ENV_FILE"; then
    esc=$(printf '%s' "$env_val" | sed 's/[|&\\]/\\&/g')
    sed -i.bak "s|^${env_key}=.*|${env_key}=${esc}|" "$ENV_FILE"
    rm -f "${ENV_FILE}.bak"
  else
    echo "${env_key}=${env_val}" >> "$ENV_FILE"
  fi
}

[ -f "$ENV_FILE" ] || exit 0

peers="$(read_env CA_PEERS)"
if is_placeholder "$peers"; then
  peers=""
fi
set_env CA_PEERS "$peers"

refresh="$(read_env CA_REFRESH_SECONDS)"
if is_placeholder "$refresh"; then
  refresh="60"
fi
case "$refresh" in
  ''|*[!0-9]*) refresh=60 ;;
esac
if [ "$refresh" -lt 15 ]; then
  refresh=15
fi
if [ "$refresh" -gt 3600 ]; then
  refresh=3600
fi
set_env CA_REFRESH_SECONDS "$refresh"

grep -v '{{' "$ENV_FILE" > "${ENV_FILE}.tmp" || true
mv "${ENV_FILE}.tmp" "$ENV_FILE"
chmod 644 "$ENV_FILE"

echo "caddy_ca_v1 env ready (peers=${peers:-none} refresh=${refresh}s)" >&2

#!/bin/sh
# Preferred entrypoint: /opt/elemento/bin/healthcheck
# Canonical path: /opt/caddy-ca/healthcheck.sh
set -eu

COMPOSE_FILE=/opt/caddy-ca/docker-compose.yml

fail() {
  echo "FAIL: $*" >&2
  exit 1
}

ok() {
  echo "OK: $*"
}

command -v docker >/dev/null 2>&1 || fail "docker not installed"
command -v curl >/dev/null 2>&1 || fail "curl not installed"

[ -f "$COMPOSE_FILE" ] || fail "missing $COMPOSE_FILE"

docker info >/dev/null 2>&1 || fail "docker daemon not reachable"

running=$(docker compose -f "$COMPOSE_FILE" ps --status running --format '{{.Service}}' 2>/dev/null || true)
echo "$running" | grep -qx caddy || fail "caddy compose service is not running"

systemctl is-active --quiet caddy-ca-collect.service \
  || fail "caddy-ca-collect.service is not active"

code=$(curl -sS -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}" --max-time 5 "http://127.0.0.1/healthz" || true)
case "$code" in
  2??) ok "CA distributor /healthz responded with $code" ;;
  *) fail "CA distributor /healthz failed (status=${code:-unreachable})" ;;
esac

cat_code=$(curl -sS -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}" --max-time 5 "http://127.0.0.1/cas.json" || true)
case "$cat_code" in
  2??) ok "CA catalog /cas.json responded with $cat_code" ;;
  *) fail "CA catalog /cas.json failed (status=${cat_code:-unreachable})" ;;
esac

ok "caddy_ca_v1 is healthy"

#!/bin/sh
# Emit service connection info as JSON on stdout.
# Preferred entrypoint: /opt/elemento/bin/service-info
# Canonical path: /opt/caddy-ca/service-info.sh
set -eu

ENV_FILE=/opt/caddy-ca/caddy-ca.env
WWW=/var/lib/caddy-ca/www

json_escape() {
  printf '%s' "$1" | sed 's/\\/\\\\/g; s/"/\\"/g'
}

pick_lan_ip() {
  for ip in $(hostname -I); do
    case "$ip" in
      *:*|127.*|172.17.*) continue ;;
    esac
    case "$ip" in
      10.*|192.168.*|172.1[6-9].*|172.2[0-9].*|172.3[0-1].*)
        echo "$ip"
        return 0
        ;;
    esac
  done
  for ip in $(hostname -I); do
    case "$ip" in
      *:*|127.*) continue ;;
      *.*.*.*)
        echo "$ip"
        return 0
        ;;
    esac
  done
  echo "127.0.0.1"
}

if [ -f "$ENV_FILE" ]; then
  # shellcheck disable=SC1090
  . "$ENV_FILE"
fi

ip="$(pick_lan_ip)"
base="http://${ip}"
ca_url="${base}/ca.crt"
catalog_url="${base}/cas.json"

count=0
if [ -f "${WWW}/ca.crt" ] && grep -q "BEGIN CERTIFICATE" "${WWW}/ca.crt"; then
  count=$(grep -c "BEGIN CERTIFICATE" "${WWW}/ca.crt" || true)
fi

peers="${CA_PEERS:-}"
echo "$peers" | grep -q '{' && peers=""

status="ready"
if [ "$count" -eq 0 ]; then
  status="waiting"
fi

cat <<EOF
{
  "api_version": "elemento.service_info/v1",
  "service": "caddy_ca_v1",
  "status": "$(json_escape "$status")",
  "endpoints": {
    "ca": "$(json_escape "$ca_url")",
    "catalog": "$(json_escape "$catalog_url")",
    "health": "$(json_escape "${base}/healthz")"
  },
  "credentials": null,
  "peers": "$(json_escape "$peers")",
  "certificate_count": ${count}
}
EOF

# Hermes Agent (`hermes_v1`)

Self-hosted [Hermes Agent](https://hermes-agent.nousresearch.com/) (Nous Research)
with a **web dashboard** and an **OpenAI-compatible API**, both behind Caddy HTTPS
(`tls internal`).

## Pair with LM Studio / OpenAI-compatible backends

```bash
python -m cloudinit_manager hermes_v1 \
  -v openai_base_url=https://<llmstudio-host>/v1 \
  -v openai_api_key=<bearer-from-llmstudio-service-info> \
  -v model=google/gemma-3n-e2b \
  -v ca_url=http://<llmstudio-ip>/ca.crt
```

Then on the VM:

```bash
sudo /opt/elemento/bin/service-info
# endpoints.ui + credentials.dashboard  → browser login
# endpoints.api + credentials.tokens[0] → OpenAI clients / Open WebUI
```

## Routing

| Path | Upstream |
|---|---|
| `https://<host>/` | Dashboard (`:9119`, Hermes basic auth) |
| `https://<host>/v1…` | OpenAI-compatible API (`:8642`, bearer) |
| `https://<host>/health` | API health |

## Other providers

```bash
# OpenRouter
python -m cloudinit_manager hermes_v1 \
  -v openrouter_api_key=sk-or-... \
  -v model=openrouter/auto

# OpenAI direct
python -m cloudinit_manager hermes_v1 \
  -v openai_api_key=sk-... \
  -v model=gpt-4o-mini
```

Leave provider vars empty to boot the gateway + dashboard only; finish setup later
with `docker exec -it hermes hermes model` (or edit `/var/lib/hermes/config.yaml`).

## Variables

| Variable | Purpose | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `openai_base_url` | Custom OpenAI-compatible base (`…/v1`) | empty |
| `openai_api_key` | Key for that base / OpenAI direct | empty |
| `openrouter_api_key` | OpenRouter key (used when no custom base) | empty |
| `model` | Default model id in `config.yaml` | provider-specific |
| `api_server_key` | Bearer for Hermes `/v1` (generated if unset) | generated |
| `api_server_model_name` | Name advertised on `/v1/models` | `hermes-agent` |
| `dashboard_username` | Dashboard basic-auth user | `hermes` |
| `dashboard_password` | Dashboard basic-auth password | generated |
| `dashboard_secret` | Session-signing secret for dashboard | generated |
| `hermes_image` | Docker image pin | `nousresearch/hermes-agent:latest` |
| `ca_url` | Peer Caddy CA (`http://<ip>/ca.crt` or [`caddy_ca_v1`](../caddy_ca_v1)) | empty |

## On-VM ops

```bash
sudo /opt/elemento/bin/healthcheck
sudo /opt/elemento/bin/service-info
docker compose -f /opt/hermes/docker-compose.yml logs -f hermes
```

## Notes

- HTTPS uses Caddy `tls internal` (same pattern as `openwebui_v1` / `llmstudio_v1`).
- Port 80 exports `GET /ca.crt` for private-IP peers. With `ca_url` set, custom
  upstreams use `ssl_verify: true`; otherwise they stay `ssl_verify: false`.
- Persistent state lives in `/var/lib/hermes` (mounted at `/opt/data` in the container).
- Unattended gateways enable `tool_loop_guardrails.hard_stop_enabled` by default.
- Dashboard auth is mandatory on non-loopback binds (Hermes security hardening).

  esac
}

# Sets PEER_CA_INSTALLED=1 when extra CA PEM was written into the bundle.
install_peer_ca() {
  ca_url=$1
  bundle=/opt/hermes/ca-bundle.pem
  extra=/opt/hermes/extra-cas.pem
  : > "$bundle"
  unset_env SSL_CERT_FILE
  PEER_CA_INSTALLED=0
  if is_placeholder "$ca_url"; then
    set_env CA_URL ""
    return 0
  fi
  url=$(normalize_ca_url "$ca_url" || true)
  if [ -z "$url" ]; then
    set_env CA_URL ""
    return 0
  fi
  pem=""
  i=0
  while [ "$i" -lt 6 ]; do
    if pem=$(fetch_pem "$url" 2>/dev/null) && echo "$pem" | grep -q "BEGIN CERTIFICATE"; then
      break
    fi
    pem=""
    i=$((i + 1))
    sleep 5
  done
  if [ -z "$pem" ]; then
    set_env CA_URL "$url"
    echo "WARN: could not fetch Caddy CA from $url" >&2
    return 0
  fi
  printf '%s\n' "$pem" > "$extra"
  if [ -f /etc/ssl/certs/ca-certificates.crt ]; then
    cat /etc/ssl/certs/ca-certificates.crt "$extra" > "$bundle"
  else
    cp "$extra" "$bundle"
  fi
  chmod 644 "$bundle"
  set_env CA_URL "$url"
  set_env SSL_CERT_FILE "/etc/ssl/hermes-ca-bundle.pem"
  PEER_CA_INSTALLED=1
  echo "Installed peer Caddy CA from $url" >&2
}

  fi
  if [ -n "$openrouter_key" ]; then

  fi

    echo "SSL_CERT_FILE=/etc/ssl/hermes-ca-bundle.pem"
  fi

chmod 600 "$DOTENV"

default_model="${model:-$model_name}"
if [ -n "$openai_base" ]; then
  cat > "$CONFIG_YAML" <<EOF

  default: '$(yaml_escape "$default_model")'
  provider: custom
  base_url: '$(yaml_escape "$openai_base")'
  api_key: '$(yaml_escape "${openai_key:-}")'
  ssl_verify: ${ssl_verify}

    idempotent_no_progress: 5

elif [ -n "$openrouter_key" ]; then
  cat > "$CONFIG_YAML" <<EOF

  default: '$(yaml_escape "${model:-openrouter/auto}")'
  provider: openrouter

fi
chmod 644 "$CONFIG_YAML"

chown -R 10000:10000 "$DATA_DIR" 2>/dev/null || true

#!/bin/sh
# Preferred entrypoint: /opt/elemento/bin/healthcheck
# Canonical path: /opt/hermes/healthcheck.sh
set -eu

COMPOSE_FILE=/opt/hermes/docker-compose.yml
ENV_FILE=/opt/hermes/hermes.env

fail() {
  echo "FAIL: $*" >&2
  exit 1
}

ok() {
  echo "OK: $*"
}

command -v docker >/dev/null 2>&1 || fail "docker not installed"
command -v curl >/dev/null 2>&1 || fail "curl not installed"

[ -f "$COMPOSE_FILE" ] || fail "missing $COMPOSE_FILE"

docker info >/dev/null 2>&1 || fail "docker daemon not reachable"

running=$(docker compose -f "$COMPOSE_FILE" ps --status running --format '{{.Service}}' 2>/dev/null || true)
echo "$running" | grep -qx hermes || fail "hermes compose service is not running"
echo "$running" | grep -qx caddy || fail "caddy compose service is not running"

if [ -f "$ENV_FILE" ]; then
  # shellcheck disable=SC1090
  . "$ENV_FILE"
fi

pick_lan_ip() {
  for ip in $(hostname -I); do
    case "$ip" in
      *:*|127.*|172.17.*) continue ;;
    esac
    case "$ip" in
      10.*|192.168.*|172.1[6-9].*|172.2[0-9].*|172.3[0-1].*)
        echo "$ip"
        return 0
        ;;
    esac
  done
  for ip in $(hostname -I); do
    case "$ip" in
      *:*|127.*) continue ;;
      *.*.*.*)
        echo "$ip"
        return 0
        ;;
    esac
  done
  echo "127.0.0.1"
}

domain="${HERMES_HOST:-}"
case "$domain" in
  ""|*\{*\}*|__HERMES_DOMAIN__|*:*)
    domain="$(pick_lan_ip).nip.io"
    ;;
esac

api_key="${API_SERVER_KEY:-}"
[ -n "$api_key" ] || fail "API_SERVER_KEY missing in $ENV_FILE"

dash_user="${HERMES_DASHBOARD_BASIC_AUTH_USERNAME:-}"
dash_pass="${HERMES_DASHBOARD_BASIC_AUTH_PASSWORD:-}"
[ -n "$dash_user" ] || fail "HERMES_DASHBOARD_BASIC_AUTH_USERNAME missing"
[ -n "$dash_pass" ] || fail "HERMES_DASHBOARD_BASIC_AUTH_PASSWORD missing"

# API probes via Caddy path routing.
code=$(curl -skS -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}" --max-time 8 \
  "https://${domain}/health" || true)
case "$code" in
  2??) ok "Caddy HTTPS /health responded with $code on https://${domain}/health" ;;
  *) fail "Caddy HTTPS /health failed for https://${domain}/health (status=${code:-unreachable})" ;;
esac

auth_code=$(curl -skS -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}" --max-time 8 \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${api_key}" \
  "https://${domain}/v1/models" || true)
case "$auth_code" in
  2??) ok "Caddy HTTPS /v1/models responded with $auth_code" ;;
  *) fail "Caddy HTTPS /v1/models failed (status=${auth_code:-unreachable})" ;;
esac

unauth_code=$(curl -skS -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}" --max-time 8 \
  "https://${domain}/v1/models" || true)
case "$unauth_code" in
  401|403) ok "API rejected unauthenticated /v1/models with $unauth_code" ;;
  *) fail "expected 401/403 without bearer, got ${unauth_code:-unreachable}" ;;
esac

# Dashboard: unauthenticated callers should be gated; basic auth should succeed.
dash_unauth=$(curl -skS -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}" --max-time 8 \
  "https://${domain}/" || true)
case "$dash_unauth" in
  401|403|302|303|307|308) ok "Dashboard gated unauthenticated request with $dash_unauth" ;;
  *) fail "expected dashboard auth gate without credentials, got ${dash_unauth:-unreachable}" ;;
esac

dash_auth=$(curl -skS -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}" --max-time 8 \
  -u "${dash_user}:${dash_pass}" \
  "https://${domain}/" || true)
case "$dash_auth" in
  2??|302|303) ok "Dashboard HTTPS responded with $dash_auth (authenticated)" ;;
  *) fail "Dashboard HTTPS check failed (status=${dash_auth:-unreachable})" ;;
esac

pem=$(curl -fsS --max-time 5 "http://127.0.0.1/ca.crt" || true)
echo "$pem" | grep -q "BEGIN CERTIFICATE" || fail "Caddy CA export missing at http://127.0.0.1/ca.crt"
ok "Caddy CA exported on http://127.0.0.1/ca.crt"

ok "hermes is healthy"

# LiteLLM Proxy (`litellm_v1`)

Self-hosted [LiteLLM Proxy](https://docs.litellm.ai/docs/simple_proxy) that
exposes one **OpenAI-compatible** HTTPS `/v1` in front of Claude, GPT, Gemini,
Groq, OpenRouter, and Elemento OpenAI-compatible peers such as
[`llmstudio_v1`](../llmstudio_v1).

## Pair with LM Studio

```bash
python -m cloudinit_manager litellm_v1 \
  -v openai_base_url=https://<llmstudio-host>/v1 \
  -v openai_api_key_local=<bearer-from-llmstudio-service-info> \
  -v local_model_id=google/gemma-3n-e2b \
  -v ca_url=http://<llmstudio-ip>/ca.crt
```

Then on the VM:

```bash
sudo /opt/elemento/bin/service-info
# endpoints.api + credentials.tokens[0] → Open WebUI / Hermes / n8n
```

Point peers at the **router**, not at LM Studio:

```bash
python -m cloudinit_manager openwebui_v1 \
  -v openai_base_url=https://<litellm-host>/v1 \
  -v openai_api_key=<litellm-master-key> \
  -v ca_url=http://<litellm-ip>/ca.crt
```

`service-info` includes copy-paste maps:

- `openwebui_v1_variables` → `-v openai_base_url=… -v openai_api_key=…`
- `hermes_v1_variables` → same, plus `-v model=…`
- `n8n_v3_variables` → `-v model_url=… -v model_api_key=… -v model_name=custom/…`

## Cloud providers

```bash
# OpenAI + Anthropic
python -m cloudinit_manager litellm_v1 \
  -v openai_api_key=sk-... \
  -v anthropic_api_key=sk-ant-...

# Local LM Studio + Claude fallback inventory
python -m cloudinit_manager litellm_v1 \
  -v openai_base_url=https://<lms-ip>.nip.io/v1 \
  -v openai_api_key_local=<lms-token> \
  -v local_model_id=google/gemma-3n-e2b \
  -v anthropic_api_key=sk-ant-... \
  -v ca_url=http://<lms-ip>/ca.crt
```

Leave provider keys empty to boot the proxy with an empty `model_list`; add
models in the **Admin UI** (`https://<host>/ui`) or re-run
`/opt/litellm/configure-litellm.sh` with provider vars, then
`docker compose -f /opt/litellm/docker-compose.yml up -d`.

## Database and Admin UI

LiteLLM requires **PostgreSQL** for DB-backed models, virtual keys, and the
Admin UI (`STORE_MODEL_IN_DB`). SQLite is **not** supported by upstream LiteLLM
(the proxy rejects non-`postgresql://` `DATABASE_URL` values).

This appliance runs a **co-located Postgres 16** container (no separate
`postgres_v1` VM). Data persists under `/var/lib/litellm/postgres`. On first boot,
`configure-litellm.sh` generates:

- `POSTGRES_PASSWORD` in `/opt/litellm/postgres.env`
- `DATABASE_URL=postgresql://litellm:…@postgres:5432/litellm` in `litellm.env`
- `LITELLM_SALT_KEY` (encrypts provider credentials added via UI — do not rotate)

Open `https://<host>/ui`, sign in with the proxy master key (`token` /
`LITELLM_MASTER_KEY`), then add or edit models without restarting the proxy.
Bootstrap models from render-time env vars still land in `config.yaml` and
coexist with UI-managed models.

## Variables

| Variable | Purpose | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `token` | Proxy master key (`Authorization: Bearer`) | generated (`sk-…`) |
| `openai_api_key` | OpenAI key(s), comma-separated for load balancing | off |
| `openai_model` / `openai_models` | Single model id, or `;`-separated list (`openai_models` wins) | `gpt-4o-mini` when key set |
| `anthropic_api_key` / `anthropic_model` / `anthropic_models` | Claude | off / `claude-sonnet-4-5` |
| `gemini_api_key` / `gemini_model` / `gemini_models` | Gemini | off / `gemini-2.0-flash` |
| `groq_api_key` / `groq_model` / `groq_models` | Groq | off / `llama-3.3-70b-versatile` |
| `openrouter_api_key` / `openrouter_model` / `openrouter_models` | OpenRouter | off / `openrouter/auto` |
| `openai_base_url` | Custom OpenAI-compatible base (`…/v1`) | empty |
| `openai_api_key_local` | Bearer(s) for that base, comma-separated | `sk-local` if URL set and key empty |
| `local_model_id` / `local_model_ids` | Model id on the custom base (`local_model_ids` is `;`-separated) | `local` |
| `litellm_image` | Docker image pin | `ghcr.io/berriai/litellm:main-stable` |
| `database_url` | Override embedded Postgres URL (advanced) | auto `postgresql://litellm:…@postgres:5432/litellm` |
| `salt_key` | Encrypts UI-stored provider keys (`LITELLM_SALT_KEY`) | generated |
| `postgres_password` | Embedded Postgres password | generated |
| `ca_url` | Peer Caddy CA (`http://<ip>/ca.crt` or [`caddy_ca_v1`](../caddy_ca_v1)) | empty |

A custom `openai_base_url` is also advertised as model id `local` when
`local_model_id` is not already `local`.

### Multiple keys and models

LiteLLM load-balances deployments that share the same `model_name`. Configure
expands provider settings into a cross product of models × keys:

```bash
# Two OpenAI models, two API keys each → four deployments, two routable names
python -m cloudinit_manager litellm_v1 \
  -v openai_api_key=sk-proj-aaa,sk-proj-bbb \
  -v openai_models='gpt-4o-mini;gpt-4o'

# Local peer: two LM Studio tokens on one model
python -m cloudinit_manager litellm_v1 \
  -v openai_base_url=https://<lms>/v1 \
  -v openai_api_key_local=token-a,token-b \
  -v local_model_id=google/gemma-3n-e2b \
  -v ca_url=http://<lms-ip>/ca.crt
```

With a single key per provider, upstream secrets stay in `litellm.env`
(`api_key: os.environ/…`). Multiple keys are written inline into `config.yaml`.

## On-VM ops

```bash
sudo /opt/elemento/bin/healthcheck
sudo /opt/elemento/bin/service-info
docker compose -f /opt/litellm/docker-compose.yml logs -f litellm
```

## Notes

- HTTPS uses Caddy `tls internal` (same pattern as `openwebui_v1` / `llmstudio_v1`).
- Port 80 exports `GET /ca.crt` for private-IP peers. With `ca_url` set, custom
  upstreams use `ssl_verify: true`; otherwise they stay `ssl_verify: false`.
- Auth is LiteLLM’s master key (not a second Caddy Bearer layer).
- Persistent copies of `config.yaml` live in `/opt/litellm` and `/var/lib/litellm`.
- Embedded Postgres data: `/var/lib/litellm/postgres`.
- UI: `https://<host>/ui` (same Bearer master key).

#!/bin/sh
# Normalize LiteLLM env, peer CA, Caddy domain, and generated config.yaml.
set -eu

ENV_FILE=/opt/litellm/litellm.env
POSTGRES_ENV=/opt/litellm/postgres.env
CADDYFILE=/opt/litellm/Caddyfile
COMPOSE_FILE=/opt/litellm/docker-compose.yml
CONFIG_YAML=/opt/litellm/config.yaml
DATA_DIR=/var/lib/litellm

is_placeholder() {
  _value=$1
  [ -z "$_value" ] && return 0
  echo "$_value" | grep -q '{' && return 0
  return 1
}

read_env() {
  env_key=$1
  grep -E "^${env_key}=" "$ENV_FILE" 2>/dev/null | tail -1 | cut -d= -f2- || true
}

generate_secret() {
  if command -v openssl >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    openssl rand -hex 32
  else
    tr -dc 'a-f0-9' </dev/urandom | head -c 64
  fi
}

set_env() {
  env_key=$1
  env_val=$2
  if grep -q "^${env_key}=" "$ENV_FILE"; then
    esc=$(printf '%s' "$env_val" | sed 's/[|&\\]/\\&/g')
    sed -i.bak "s|^${env_key}=.*|${env_key}=${esc}|" "$ENV_FILE"
    rm -f "${ENV_FILE}.bak"
  else
    echo "${env_key}=${env_val}" >> "$ENV_FILE"
  fi
}

unset_env() {
  env_key=$1
  if grep -q "^${env_key}=" "$ENV_FILE"; then
    grep -v "^${env_key}=" "$ENV_FILE" > "${ENV_FILE}.tmp" || true
    mv "${ENV_FILE}.tmp" "$ENV_FILE"
  fi
}

yaml_escape() {
  printf '%s' "$1" | sed "s/'/''/g"
}

# Comma-separated keys (whitespace trimmed). Prints one key per line.
split_keys() {
  _csv=$1
  OLDIFS=$IFS
  IFS=,
  for _k in $_csv; do
    _k=$(echo "$_k" | sed 's/^[[:space:]]*//; s/[[:space:]]*$//')
    [ -n "$_k" ] || continue
    printf '%s\n' "$_k"
  done
  IFS=$OLDIFS
}

# Semicolon-separated model ids, else a single default. Prints one id per line.
resolve_model_ids() {
  _models_list=$1
  _single=$2
  _default=$3
  if [ -n "$_models_list" ]; then
    OLDIFS=$IFS
    IFS=';'
    for _m in $_models_list; do
      _m=$(echo "$_m" | sed 's/^[[:space:]]*//; s/[[:space:]]*$//')
      [ -n "$_m" ] || continue
      printf '%s\n' "$_m"
    done
    IFS=$OLDIFS
    return 0
  fi
  if [ -n "$_single" ]; then
    printf '%s\n' "$_single"
    return 0
  fi
  if [ -n "$_default" ]; then
    printf '%s\n' "$_default"
  fi
}

pick_lan_ip() {
  for ip in $(hostname -I); do
    case "$ip" in
      *:*|127.*|172.17.*) continue ;;
    esac
    case "$ip" in
      10.*|192.168.*|172.1[6-9].*|172.2[0-9].*|172.3[0-1].*)
        echo "$ip"
        return 0
        ;;
    esac
  done
  for ip in $(hostname -I); do
    case "$ip" in
      *:*|127.*) continue ;;
      *.*.*.*)
        echo "$ip"
        return 0
        ;;
    esac
  done
  echo "127.0.0.1"
}

normalize_ca_url() {
  u=$1
  [ -n "$u" ] || return 1
  echo "$u" | grep -q '{' && return 1
  case "$u" in
    http://*|https://*)
      case "$u" in
        */ca.crt|*/cas.json|*.pem|*.crt) printf '%s\n' "$u" ;;
        */) printf '%sca.crt\n' "$u" ;;
        *) printf '%s/ca.crt\n' "$u" ;;
      esac
      ;;
    *) printf 'http://%s/ca.crt\n' "$u" ;;
  esac
}

fetch_pem() {
  url=$1
  case "$url" in
    https://*) curl -fskS --max-time 10 "$url" ;;
    *) curl -fsS --max-time 10 "$url" ;;
  esac
}

# Sets PEER_CA_INSTALLED=1 when extra CA PEM was written into the bundle.
install_peer_ca() {
  ca_url=$1
  bundle=/opt/litellm/ca-bundle.pem
  extra=/opt/litellm/extra-cas.pem
  : > "$bundle"
  unset_env SSL_CERT_FILE
  unset_env REQUESTS_CA_BUNDLE
  PEER_CA_INSTALLED=0
  if is_placeholder "$ca_url"; then
    set_env CA_URL ""
    return 0
  fi
  url=$(normalize_ca_url "$ca_url" || true)
  if [ -z "$url" ]; then
    set_env CA_URL ""
    return 0
  fi
  pem=""
  i=0
  while [ "$i" -lt 6 ]; do
    if pem=$(fetch_pem "$url" 2>/dev/null) && echo "$pem" | grep -q "BEGIN CERTIFICATE"; then
      break
    fi
    pem=""
    i=$((i + 1))
    sleep 5
  done
  if [ -z "$pem" ]; then
    set_env CA_URL "$url"
    echo "WARN: could not fetch Caddy CA from $url" >&2
    return 0
  fi
  printf '%s\n' "$pem" > "$extra"
  if [ -f /etc/ssl/certs/ca-certificates.crt ]; then
    cat /etc/ssl/certs/ca-certificates.crt "$extra" > "$bundle"
  else
    cp "$extra" "$bundle"
  fi
  chmod 644 "$bundle"
  set_env CA_URL "$url"
  set_env SSL_CERT_FILE "/etc/ssl/litellm-ca-bundle.pem"
  set_env REQUESTS_CA_BUNDLE "/etc/ssl/litellm-ca-bundle.pem"
  PEER_CA_INSTALLED=1
  echo "Installed peer Caddy CA from $url" >&2
}

postgres_user="litellm"

postgres_password=""
if [ -f "$POSTGRES_ENV" ]; then

if is_placeholder "$postgres_user"; then postgres_user="litellm"; fi

salt_key="$(read_env LITELLM_SALT_KEY)"
if is_placeholder "$salt_key"; then

fi

master_key="$(read_env LITELLM_MASTER_KEY)"

litellm_image="$(read_env LITELLM_IMAGE)"

fi
set_env LITELLM_IMAGE "$litellm_image"

openai_key="$(read_env OPENAI_API_KEY)"
openai_model="$(read_env OPENAI_MODEL)"
openai_models="$(read_env OPENAI_MODELS)"
anthropic_key="$(read_env ANTHROPIC_API_KEY)"
anthropic_model="$(read_env ANTHROPIC_MODEL)"
anthropic_models="$(read_env ANTHROPIC_MODELS)"
gemini_key="$(read_env GEMINI_API_KEY)"
gemini_model="$(read_env GEMINI_MODEL)"
gemini_models="$(read_env GEMINI_MODELS)"
groq_key="$(read_env GROQ_API_KEY)"
groq_model="$(read_env GROQ_MODEL)"
groq_models="$(read_env GROQ_MODELS)"
openrouter_key="$(read_env OPENROUTER_API_KEY)"
openrouter_model="$(read_env OPENROUTER_MODEL)"
openrouter_models="$(read_env OPENROUTER_MODELS)"
openai_base="$(read_env OPENAI_BASE_URL)"
openai_key_local="$(read_env OPENAI_API_KEY_LOCAL)"
local_model_id="$(read_env LOCAL_MODEL_ID)"
local_model_ids="$(read_env LOCAL_MODEL_IDS)"

if is_placeholder "$openai_key"; then openai_key=""; fi
if is_placeholder "$openai_model"; then openai_model=""; fi
if is_placeholder "$openai_models"; then openai_models=""; fi
if is_placeholder "$anthropic_key"; then anthropic_key=""; fi

if is_placeholder "$local_model_id"; then local_model_id=""; fi
if is_placeholder "$local_model_ids"; then local_model_ids=""; fi

set_env OPENAI_API_KEY "$openai_key"
set_env OPENAI_MODEL "$openai_model"
set_env OPENAI_MODELS "$openai_models"
set_env ANTHROPIC_API_KEY "$anthropic_key"

set_env GEMINI_API_KEY "$gemini_key"

set_env GROQ_API_KEY "$groq_key"

PEER_CA_INSTALLED=0
install_peer_ca "$(read_env CA_URL)"

if [ -z "$domain" ] || echo "$domain" | grep -q '__LITELLM_DOMAIN__\|{\|:'; then

fi

models_yaml=""
model_names=""
deployment_count=0

append_name() {

  fi

  else

}

add_deployment() {
  _name=$1
  _litellm_model=$2
  _api_key=$3
  _key_env=$4
  _extra=$5
  deployment_count=$((deployment_count + 1))

  elif [ -n "$_key_env" ]; then
    _key_line="      api_key: os.environ/${_key_env}"
  else
    echo "internal error: add_deployment needs api_key or key_env" >&2
    exit 1
  fi
  models_yaml="${models_yaml}
  - model_name: '$(yaml_escape "$_name")'
    litellm_params:
      model: '$(yaml_escape "$_litellm_model")'
${_key_line}"
  if [ -n "$_extra" ]; then
    models_yaml="${models_yaml}
${_extra}"
  fi
  append_name "$_name"
}

# keys_csv: comma-separated upstream keys. models_list: semicolon-separated ids.
add_provider_deployments() {
  _provider=$1
  _keys_csv=$2
  _models_list=$3
  _single_model=$4
  _default_model=$5
  _key_env=$6

  [ -n "$_keys_csv" ] || return 0

  _keys_file=$(mktemp)
  _models_file=$(mktemp)
  split_keys "$_keys_csv" > "$_keys_file"
  resolve_model_ids "$_models_list" "$_single_model" "$_default_model" > "$_models_file"

  _key_count=0
  while IFS= read -r _k || [ -n "$_k" ]; do
    [ -n "$_k" ] || continue
    _key_count=$((_key_count + 1))
  done < "$_keys_file"

  while IFS= read -r _mid || [ -n "$_mid" ]; do
    [ -n "$_mid" ] || continue
    if [ "$_provider" = "openrouter" ]; then
      _litellm_model="openrouter/${_mid#openrouter/}"
    else
      _litellm_model="${_provider}/${_mid}"
    fi
    if [ "$_key_count" -eq 1 ]; then
      add_deployment "$_mid" "$_litellm_model" "" "$_key_env" ""
    else
      while IFS= read -r _k || [ -n "$_k" ]; do
        [ -n "$_k" ] || continue
        add_deployment "$_mid" "$_litellm_model" "$_k" "" ""
      done < "$_keys_file"
    fi
  done < "$_models_file"

  rm -f "$_keys_file" "$_models_file"
}

add_provider_deployments openai "$openai_key" "$openai_models" "$openai_model" "gpt-4o-mini" "OPENAI_API_KEY"
add_provider_deployments anthropic "$anthropic_key" "$anthropic_models" "$anthropic_model" "claude-sonnet-4-5" "ANTHROPIC_API_KEY"

if [ -n "$openai_base" ]; then
  if [ -z "$openai_key_local" ]; then
    openai_key_local="sk-local"
    set_env OPENAI_API_KEY_LOCAL "$openai_key_local"
    echo "WARN: OPENAI_BASE_URL is set but OPENAI_API_KEY_LOCAL is empty; using sk-local" >&2
  fi
  local_extra="      api_base: '$(yaml_escape "$openai_base")'
      ssl_verify: ${ssl_verify}"
  _local_keys_file=$(mktemp)
  _local_models_file=$(mktemp)
  split_keys "$openai_key_local" > "$_local_keys_file"
  resolve_model_ids "$local_model_ids" "$local_model_id" "local" > "$_local_models_file"

  _local_key_count=0
  while IFS= read -r _k || [ -n "$_k" ]; do
    [ -n "$_k" ] || continue
    _local_key_count=$((_local_key_count + 1))
  done < "$_local_keys_file"

  while IFS= read -r _lid || [ -n "$_lid" ]; do
    [ -n "$_lid" ] || continue
    _litellm_local="openai/${_lid}"
    if [ "$_local_key_count" -eq 1 ]; then
      add_deployment "$_lid" "$_litellm_local" "" "OPENAI_API_KEY_LOCAL" "$local_extra"
      if [ "$_lid" != "local" ]; then
        add_deployment "local" "$_litellm_local" "" "OPENAI_API_KEY_LOCAL" "$local_extra"
      fi
    else
      while IFS= read -r _k || [ -n "$_k" ]; do
        [ -n "$_k" ] || continue
        add_deployment "$_lid" "$_litellm_local" "$_k" "" "$local_extra"
      done < "$_local_keys_file"
      if [ "$_lid" != "local" ]; then
        while IFS= read -r _k || [ -n "$_k" ]; do
          [ -n "$_k" ] || continue
          add_deployment "local" "$_litellm_local" "$_k" "" "$local_extra"
        done < "$_local_keys_file"
      fi
    fi
  done < "$_local_models_file"
  rm -f "$_local_keys_file" "$_local_models_file"
fi

set_env LITELLM_MODEL_NAMES "$model_names"

router_yaml=""
if [ "$deployment_count" -gt 1 ]; then
  router_yaml="
router_settings:
  routing_strategy: simple-shuffle"
fi

if [ -z "$models_yaml" ]; then
  cat > "$CONFIG_YAML" <<EOF
model_list: []
general_settings:
  master_key: os.environ/LITELLM_MASTER_KEY
  store_model_in_db: true
  database_url: os.environ/DATABASE_URL
EOF
  echo "WARN: no provider keys / OPENAI_BASE_URL — proxy will start with an empty model_list (add models in Admin UI)" >&2
else
  cat > "$CONFIG_YAML" <<EOF
model_list:${models_yaml}${router_yaml}
general_settings:
  master_key: os.environ/LITELLM_MASTER_KEY
  store_model_in_db: true
  database_url: os.environ/DATABASE_URL
EOF
fi
chmod 600 "$CONFIG_YAML"
cp "$CONFIG_YAML" "${DATA_DIR}/config.yaml"
chmod 600 "${DATA_DIR}/config.yaml"

grep -v '{{' "$ENV_FILE" > "${ENV_FILE}.tmp" || true
mv "${ENV_FILE}.tmp" "$ENV_FILE"
chmod 600 "$ENV_FILE"

echo "LiteLLM env ready (domain=${domain} models=${model_names:-none} openai_base=${openai_base:-none} db=postgres)" >&2

services:
  postgres:
    image: postgres:16
    restart: unless-stopped
    env_file:
      - /opt/litellm/postgres.env
    volumes:
      - /var/lib/litellm/postgres:/var/lib/postgresql/data
    expose:
      - "5432"
    healthcheck:

    depends_on:

    volumes:
      - /opt/litellm/config.yaml:/app/config.yaml:ro

files.README.md:
# LM Studio (`llmstudio_v1`)

Headless LM Studio appliance: local OpenAI-compatible API on `127.0.0.1:1234`, optional Caddy HTTPS reverse proxy with Bearer auth on `:443`.

Version: **1.5.0**

## Template variables

| Variable | Env key | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `LMS_MODEL_ID` | `LMS_MODEL_ID` | Model to download and load (e.g. `openai/gpt-oss-20b`) |
| `token` | `LMS_API_TOKEN` | One Bearer token, or a comma-separated list |
| `token_count` | `LMS_API_TOKEN_COUNT` | How many tokens to generate on the instance when `token` is unset (default `1`, max `32`) |

Render examples:

```bash
# Inject a single token
python -m cloudinit_manager llmstudio_v1 -v LMS_MODEL_ID=openai/gpt-oss-20b -v token=my-secret

# Inject several tokens (any one is accepted)
python -m cloudinit_manager llmstudio_v1 -v LMS_MODEL_ID=openai/gpt-oss-20b -v token=alice-secret,bob-secret

# Generate 3 tokens on first boot (no -v token=...)
python -m cloudinit_manager llmstudio_v1 -v LMS_MODEL_ID=openai/gpt-oss-20b -v token_count=3
```

## Authentication (Caddy)

LM Studio has no native API token support. When `LMS_ENABLE_CADDY=true` (default in this service), `configure-caddy.sh` writes a Caddyfile that:

1. Listens on `:443` for every instance IP as `<ip>.nip.io` (plus a bare `:443` catch-all)
2. Uses `tls internal` (self-signed / local CA)
3. Rejects requests without a valid `Authorization: Bearer <token>` with **401**
4. Proxies authorized traffic to `127.0.0.1:1234`

Multiple tokens are expressed as AND-ed `not header` matchers: a request is unauthorized only if it matches **none** of the configured tokens.

The local bind `http://127.0.0.1:1234` stays open without Bearer auth (same host only).

### Token resolution order

On each `configure-caddy.sh` run (also as `ExecStartPre` for `lmstudio.service`):

1. **Existing** `/opt/llmstudio/api-tokens` (if non-empty) — reused across restarts
2. Else **`LMS_API_TOKEN`** from `/opt/llmstudio/lmstudio.env` (injected `token`, possibly comma-separated)
3. Else **generate** `LMS_API_TOKEN_COUNT` tokens with `openssl rand -hex 32`

Generated / resolved tokens are always written back to:

| Path | Format | Mode |
|---|---|---|
| `/opt/llmstudio/api-tokens` | one token per line | `0600` |
| `/opt/llmstudio/lmstudio.env` → `LMS_API_TOKEN` | comma-separated | updated in place |

### Calling the API

Preferred: dump connection info (endpoints + bearer tokens) as JSON:

```bash
sudo /opt/elemento/bin/service-info
```

Or manually:

```bash
TOKEN=$(sudo head -n1 /opt/llmstudio/api-tokens)
DOMAIN=$(grep '^LMS_CADDY_DOMAIN=' /opt/llmstudio/lmstudio.env | cut -d= -f2)

curl -sk -H "Authorization: Bearer ${TOKEN}" "https://${DOMAIN}/v1/models"
```

List all accepted tokens:

```bash
sudo cat /opt/llmstudio/api-tokens
```

### Rotating tokens

1. Replace `/opt/llmstudio/api-tokens` (one token per line) **or** set `LMS_API_TOKEN` in `lmstudio.env` and remove the tokens file
2. Re-run configure and reload Caddy:

```bash
sudo /opt/llmstudio/configure-caddy.sh
sudo docker compose -f /opt/llmstudio/docker-compose.caddy.yml up -d
```

## Networking & prerequisites

| Port | Role |
|---|---|
| `1234/tcp` | LM Studio API (bound to localhost) |
| `443/tcp` | Caddy HTTPS proxy |

Storage: `/home/ubuntu/.lmstudio` (min 20 GB). Baseline resources: 4 vCPU, 8 GB RAM.

## Layout on the instance

| Path | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `/opt/llmstudio/lmstudio.env` | Runtime env (model id, tokens, Caddy domain) |
| `/opt/llmstudio/configure-caddy.sh` | Builds Caddyfile + resolves/generates tokens |
| `/opt/llmstudio/Caddyfile` | Generated proxy config |
| `/opt/llmstudio/docker-compose.caddy.yml` | Caddy container |
| `/opt/llmstudio/api-tokens` | Accepted Bearer tokens (one per line) |
| `/opt/llmstudio/healthcheck.sh` | Readiness probe (API + Caddy 401/2xx) |
| `/opt/llmstudio/service-info.sh` | JSON endpoints + credentials for operators/runtimes |
| `/opt/elemento/bin/healthcheck` | Symlink → healthcheck.sh |
| `/opt/elemento/bin/service-info` | Symlink → service-info.sh |
| `/opt/llmstudio/lmstudio-start.sh` | Bootstrap: get/load model, start server, start Caddy |
| `/etc/systemd/system/lmstudio.service` | Supervises bootstrap / server |

## Operations

```bash
# Service status / logs
systemctl status lmstudio.service
journalctl -u lmstudio.service -f
tail -f /var/log/lmstudio-bootstrap.log

# Caddy logs
docker compose -f /opt/llmstudio/docker-compose.caddy.yml logs -f caddy

# Healthcheck / service info (stable entrypoints)
sudo /opt/elemento/bin/healthcheck
sudo /opt/elemento/bin/service-info
```

Healthcheck expectations when Caddy is enabled:

- unauthenticated `GET /v1/models` over HTTPS → **401**
- same request with a valid Bearer token → **2xx**

## TLS note for clients

Caddy uses an internal CA (`tls internal`). Clients that verify certificates (e.g. Node / n8n) need that CA, or must use a trust override.

On private-IP deployments the root CA is exported over HTTP (no TLS chicken-and-egg):

```bash
curl -fsS http://<this-host>/ca.crt
# also in service-info as endpoints.ca
```

Pass that URL to peer services as `ca_url`, or aggregate several peers with [`caddy_ca_v1`](../caddy_ca_v1).

The CA still lives in the Caddy data volume:

```bash
docker compose -f /opt/llmstudio/docker-compose.caddy.yml exec caddy \
  cat /data/caddy/pki/authorities/local/root.crt
```

`curl -sk` skips verification for ad-hoc checks.

files.files/configure-caddy.sh:
#!/bin/sh
set -eu

ENV_FILE=/opt/llmstudio/lmstudio.env
CADDYFILE=/opt/llmstudio/Caddyfile
TOKENS_FILE=/opt/llmstudio/api-tokens

if [ -f "$ENV_FILE" ]; then
  # shellcheck disable=SC1090
  . "$ENV_FILE"
fi

if [ "${LMS_ENABLE_CADDY:-false}" != "true" ]; then
  exit 0
fi

PORT="${LMS_SERVER_PORT:-1234}"
UPSTREAM="${LMS_SERVER_HOST:-127.0.0.1}"
TOKEN="${LMS_API_TOKEN:-}"
TOKEN_COUNT="${LMS_API_TOKEN_COUNT:-1}"

set_env() {
  key=$1
  value=$2
  if grep -q "^${key}=" "$ENV_FILE"; then
    sed -i.bak "s|^${key}=.*|${key}=${value}|" "$ENV_FILE"
    rm -f "${ENV_FILE}.bak"
  else
    echo "${key}=${value}" >> "$ENV_FILE"
  fi
}

generate_token() {
  if command -v openssl >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    openssl rand -hex 32
  else
    tr -dc 'a-f0-9' </dev/urandom | head -c 64
  fi
}

# Normalize count: missing/placeholder -> 1; clamp to a sane range.
case "$TOKEN_COUNT" in
  ''|*[!0-9]*|*'{'*) TOKEN_COUNT=1 ;;
esac
if [ "$TOKEN_COUNT" -lt 1 ]; then
  TOKEN_COUNT=1
fi
if [ "$TOKEN_COUNT" -gt 32 ]; then
  TOKEN_COUNT=32
fi

# Prefer an existing tokens file (idempotent across restarts), then env,
# otherwise generate N tokens on the box.
if [ -f "$TOKENS_FILE" ] && [ -s "$TOKENS_FILE" ]; then
  TOKEN=$(tr '\n' ',' < "$TOKENS_FILE" | sed 's/,$//')
elif [ -z "$TOKEN" ] || echo "$TOKEN" | grep -q '{'; then
  echo "LMS_API_TOKEN unset; generating ${TOKEN_COUNT} token(s) on the instance" >&2
  generated=""
  i=0
  while [ "$i" -lt "$TOKEN_COUNT" ]; do
    t=$(generate_token)
    if [ -n "$generated" ]; then
      generated="${generated},${t}"
    else
      generated="$t"
    fi
    i=$((i + 1))
  done
  TOKEN="$generated"
fi

# Persist one token per line for operators; rewrite Caddy matchers from this list.
umask 077
printf '%s\n' "$TOKEN" | tr ',' '\n' | sed '/^$/d' > "$TOKENS_FILE"
chmod 600 "$TOKENS_FILE"
TOKEN=$(tr '\n' ',' < "$TOKENS_FILE" | sed 's/,$//')
set_env LMS_API_TOKEN "$TOKEN"

unauthorized_matchers=""
while IFS= read -r t; do
  [ -n "$t" ] || continue
  unauthorized_matchers="${unauthorized_matchers}
        not header Authorization \"Bearer ${t}\""
done < "$TOKENS_FILE"

if [ -z "$unauthorized_matchers" ]; then
  echo "No API tokens available for Caddy Bearer auth" >&2
  exit 1
fi

meta() {
  curl -fsS --max-time 2 -H "Metadata-Flavor: Google" \
    "http://metadata.google.internal/computeMetadata/v1/$1" 2>/dev/null || true
}

add_ip() {
  ip=$1
  [ -n "$ip" ] || return 0
  echo "$ip" | grep -Eq '^[0-9]{1,3}(\.[0-9]{1,3}){3}$' || return 0
  case "$ip" in
    127.*) return 0 ;;
  esac
  echo "$ip"
}

is_private() {
  case "$1" in
    10.*|192.168.*|172.1[6-9].*|172.2[0-9].*|172.3[0-1].*) return 0 ;;
    *) return 1 ;;
  esac
}

# Docker installs docker0 (172.17.0.1) before the LAN NIC; skip it for primary domain.
is_docker_bridge() {
  case "$1" in
    172.17.*) return 0 ;;
    *) return 1 ;;
  esac
}

ips=$(
  {
    hostname -I | tr ' ' '\n'
    meta instance/network-interfaces/ | tr '/' '\n' | grep -E '^[0-9]+$' | while read -r nic; do
      add_ip "$(meta "instance/network-interfaces/${nic}/ip")"
      meta "instance/network-interfaces/${nic}/access-configs/" | tr '/' '\n' | grep -E '^[0-9]+$' | while read -r ac; do
        add_ip "$(meta "instance/network-interfaces/${nic}/access-configs/${ac}/external-ip")"
      done
    done
  } | while read -r ip; do
    add_ip "$ip"
  done | sort -u
)

addrs=":443"
public_domain=""
private_domain=""
for ip in $ips; do
  addrs="${addrs}, ${ip}.nip.io"
  if is_private "$ip" && ! is_docker_bridge "$ip"; then
    [ -n "$private_domain" ] || private_domain="${ip}.nip.io"
  elif ! is_private "$ip"; then
    [ -n "$public_domain" ] || public_domain="${ip}.nip.io"
  fi
done
primary="${public_domain:-$private_domain}"

# LM Studio has no native API token support; enforce Bearer auth at the proxy.
# Multiple "not header" lines are ANDed: unauthorized only if none of the tokens match.
# :80 exports the tls-internal root CA so private-IP peers can trust this instance.
# auto_https disable_redirects keeps http://<ip>/ca.crt from 308'ing to HTTPS.
cat > "$CADDYFILE" <<EOF
{
  auto_https disable_redirects
}

:80 {
    handle /ca.crt {
        root * /data/caddy/pki/authorities/local
        rewrite * /root.crt
        header Content-Type application/x-pem-file
        file_server
    }
    handle {
        respond "Elemento Caddy CA export. GET /ca.crt" 200
    }
}

${addrs} {
    tls internal
    @unauthorized {${unauthorized_matchers}
    }
    respond @unauthorized "Unauthorized" 401
    reverse_proxy ${UPSTREAM}:${PORT}
}
EOF

if [ -n "$primary" ]; then
  set_env LMS_CADDY_DOMAIN "$primary"
fi

ok() {
  echo "OK: $*"
}

  . "$ENV_FILE"

pick_lan_ip() {
  for ip in $(hostname -I); do
    case "$ip" in
      *:*|127.*|172.17.*) continue ;;
    esac
    case "$ip" in
      10.*|192.168.*|172.1[6-9].*|172.2[0-9].*|172.3[0-1].*)
        echo "$ip"
        return 0
        ;;
    esac
  done
  for ip in $(hostname -I); do
    case "$ip" in
      *:*|127.*) continue ;;
      *.*.*.*)
        echo "$ip"
        return 0
        ;;
    esac
  done
  echo "127.0.0.1"
}

command -v systemctl >/dev/null 2>&1 || fail "systemctl not available"

systemctl is-active --quiet lmstudio.service || fail "lmstudio.service is not active"

code=$(curl -sS -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}" --max-time 5 \
  "http://127.0.0.1:${PORT}/v1/models" || true)
case "$code" in
  2??) ok "LM Studio API responded with $code on :${PORT}/v1/models" ;;
  *) fail "LM Studio API check failed (status=${code:-unreachable})" ;;
esac

if [ "$ENABLE_CADDY" = "true" ]; then
  command -v docker >/dev/null 2>&1 || fail "docker not installed (required when Caddy is enabled)"

  docker compose -f /opt/llmstudio/docker-compose.caddy.yml ps --status running --format '{{.Service}}' 2>/dev/null \
    | grep -qx caddy || fail "caddy compose service is not running"

    TOKEN=$(head -n 1 "$TOKENS_FILE")
  else
    # Comma-separated list from env: use the first token for the probe.
    TOKEN=$(printf '%s' "$TOKEN" | tr ',' '\n' | sed '/^$/d' | head -n 1)
  fi
  [ -n "$TOKEN" ] && ! echo "$TOKEN" | grep -q '{' || fail "LMS_API_TOKEN is not set"

  # Probe a hostname on the tls-internal cert (not https://127.0.0.1 — SNI mismatch).
  domain="${LMS_CADDY_DOMAIN:-}"
  if [ -z "$domain" ] || echo "$domain" | grep -q ':' ; then
    domain="$(pick_lan_ip).nip.io"
  fi

  unauth_code=$(curl -skS -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}" --max-time 5 \
    "https://${domain}/v1/models" || true)
  case "$unauth_code" in
    401) ok "Caddy rejected unauthenticated request with 401" ;;
    *) fail "Caddy auth check failed for https://${domain}/v1/models (expected 401, got ${unauth_code:-unreachable})" ;;
  esac

    -H "Authorization: Bearer ${TOKEN}" \
    "https://${domain}/v1/models" || true)
  case "$caddy_code" in
    2??) ok "Caddy HTTPS responded with $caddy_code on https://${domain}/v1/models" ;;
    *) fail "Caddy HTTPS check failed for https://${domain}/v1/models (status=${caddy_code:-unreachable})" ;;
  esac

  pem=$(curl -fsS --max-time 5 "http://127.0.0.1/ca.crt" || true)
  echo "$pem" | grep -q "BEGIN CERTIFICATE" || fail "Caddy CA export missing at http://127.0.0.1/ca.crt"
  ok "Caddy CA exported on http://127.0.0.1/ca.crt"

#!/bin/sh
set -eu

LMS=/home/ubuntu/.lmstudio/bin/lms
LOG_PREFIX="[lmstudio-bootstrap]"

log() {
  echo "$LOG_PREFIX $*"
}

run_lms() {
  attempt=1
  while [ "$attempt" -le 10 ]; do
    if "$LMS" "$@"; then
      return 0
    fi
    log "command failed: lms $* (attempt ${attempt}/10)"
    sleep 3
    attempt=$((attempt + 1))
  done
  return 1
}

model_configured() {
  [ -n "${LMS_MODEL_ID:-}" ] && ! echo "$LMS_MODEL_ID" | grep -q '{'
}

log "phase 1: verifying dependencies"
if [ ! -x "$LMS" ]; then
  log "lms binary not found at $LMS"
  exit 1
fi

log "phase 2: starting llmster daemon"
run_lms daemon up
sleep 3

if model_configured; then
  log "phase 3: downloading model ${LMS_MODEL_ID}"
  run_lms get "$LMS_MODEL_ID"
  log "phase 4: loading model ${LMS_MODEL_ID}"
  run_lms load "$LMS_MODEL_ID" --yes
else
  log "phase 3-4: skipped (no LMS_MODEL_ID configured)"
fi

log "phase 5: starting API server on ${LMS_SERVER_HOST}:${LMS_SERVER_PORT}"
run_lms server start --bind "$LMS_SERVER_HOST" --port "$LMS_SERVER_PORT"

log "phase 5: verifying API server"
ready=0
for _ in $(seq 1 60); do
  if curl -sf "http://127.0.0.1:${LMS_SERVER_PORT}/v1/models" >/dev/null; then
    ready=1
    break
  fi
  sleep 2
done
if [ "$ready" -ne 1 ]; then
  log "API server did not become ready on port ${LMS_SERVER_PORT}"
  exit 1
fi

if [ "${LMS_ENABLE_CADDY:-false}" = "true" ]; then
  log "phase 6: starting Caddy reverse proxy on all instance IPs"
  docker compose -f /opt/llmstudio/docker-compose.caddy.yml up -d
fi

log "bootstrap complete"

- Data: `/var/lib/mysql`.
- `service-info` exposes `credentials.uri` (`mysql://…`) plus discrete fields.

#!/bin/sh
# Normalize MariaDB env: mint passwords when placeholder/empty.
set -eu

ENV_FILE=/opt/mariadb/mariadb.env

is_placeholder() {
  _value=$1
  [ -z "$_value" ] && return 0
  echo "$_value" | grep -q '{' && return 0
  return 1
}

read_env() {
  env_key=$1
  grep -E "^${env_key}=" "$ENV_FILE" 2>/dev/null | tail -1 | cut -d= -f2- || true
}

generate_secret() {
  if command -v openssl >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    openssl rand -hex 32
  else
    tr -dc 'a-f0-9' </dev/urandom | head -c 64
  fi
}

set_env() {
  env_key=$1
  env_val=$2
  if grep -q "^${env_key}=" "$ENV_FILE"; then
    esc=$(printf '%s' "$env_val" | sed 's/[|&\\]/\\&/g')
    sed -i.bak "s|^${env_key}=.*|${env_key}=${esc}|" "$ENV_FILE"
    rm -f "${ENV_FILE}.bak"
  else
    echo "${env_key}=${env_val}" >> "$ENV_FILE"
  fi
}

[ -f "$ENV_FILE" ] || exit 0

root_password="$(read_env MYSQL_ROOT_PASSWORD)"
if is_placeholder "$root_password"; then
  root_password=$(generate_secret)
fi
set_env MYSQL_ROOT_PASSWORD "$root_password"

password="$(read_env MYSQL_PASSWORD)"
if is_placeholder "$password"; then
  password=$(generate_secret)
fi
set_env MYSQL_PASSWORD "$password"

user="$(read_env MYSQL_USER)"
if is_placeholder "$user"; then
  user=elemento
fi
set_env MYSQL_USER "$user"

db="$(read_env MYSQL_DATABASE)"
if is_placeholder "$db"; then
  db=elemento
fi
set_env MYSQL_DATABASE "$db"

grep -v '{{' "$ENV_FILE" > "${ENV_FILE}.tmp" || true
mv "${ENV_FILE}.tmp" "$ENV_FILE"
chmod 600 "$ENV_FILE"

echo "MariaDB env ready (user=${user} db=${db})" >&2

# MongoDB (`mongodb_v1`)

[MongoDB](https://www.mongodb.com/) 7 with root auth enabled. Native TCP on
port **27017** (no Caddy) for peer clients.

## Launch

```bash
python -m cloudinit_manager mongodb_v1
# optional: -v password=my-secret
```

On the VM:

```bash
sudo /opt/elemento/bin/healthcheck
sudo /opt/elemento/bin/service-info
```

## Variables

| Variable | Purpose | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `password` | `MONGO_INITDB_ROOT_PASSWORD` | generated on first boot |

Default root username: `elemento` (`authSource=admin`).

## Notes

- Image: `mongo:7` (pinned).
- Data: `/var/lib/mongo`.
- `service-info` exposes `credentials.uri` (`mongodb://…/?authSource=admin`).

# n8n AI Sandbox Runner (`n8n_runner_v1`)

Separate VM appliance that runs n8n’s **AI Assistant sandbox** stack
(`sandbox-api` + privileged DinD `sandbox-runner-1`). Pair it with
[`n8n_v3`](../n8n_v3) (and optionally [`llmstudio_v1`](../llmstudio_v1) as the
OpenAI-compatible model).

This is **not** the Code-node `n8nio/runners` task-runner image. It is the
sandbox the editor asks for when enabling Instance AI / AI Assistant.

## Two-VM flow

```text
┌─────────────────────┐         HTTP :8080 + API key        ┌──────────────────────┐
│  n8n_v3             │ ──────────────────────────────────► │  n8n_runner_v1       │
│  (+ Caddy :443)     │                                     │  sandbox-api :8080   │
│                     │         HTTPS OpenAI-compat          │  sandbox-runner DinD │
│  optional model ────┼──────────────────────────────────►  │  (internal only)     │
│  llmstudio_v1       │                                     └──────────────────────┘
└─────────────────────┘
```

1. Launch **n8n_runner_v1** first.
2. After healthcheck passes, read connection info:

   ```bash
   sudo /opt/elemento/bin/service-info
   ```

3. Launch **n8n_v3** with the returned values (and a model endpoint):

   ```bash
   python -m cloudinit_manager n8n_v3 \
     -v sandbox_api_url=http://<runner-ip>:8080 \
     -v sandbox_api_key=<api_key_from_service_info> \
     -v model_url=https://<llmstudio-host>/v1 \
     -v model_api_key=<bearer-token> \
     -v model_name=google/gemma-3n-e2b \
     -v ca_url=http://<llmstudio-ip>/ca.crt
   ```

   `configure-ai.sh` also sets `N8N_SANDBOX_SERVICE_URL` /
   `N8N_SANDBOX_SERVICE_API_KEY` (required by current n8n for
   `provider=n8n-sandbox`) and rewrites LM Studio model ids to
   `custom/<id>` so Instance AI uses the OpenAI-compatible endpoint instead of
   the built-in Google/OpenAI providers.

4. Restrict firewall on the runner so **:8080** is only reachable from the n8n
   VM (or a private network). Do not expose DinD / gRPC ports publicly.

For a full Multipass walkthrough (LM Studio + runner + `caddy_ca_v1` + n8n),
see [`examples/multipass-n8n-runner-llmstudio-ca.sh`](../../examples/multipass-n8n-runner-llmstudio-ca.sh).

## Layout on the instance

| Path | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `/opt/n8n-runner/docker-compose.yml` | certs + api + runner |
| `/opt/n8n-runner/runner.env` | sandbox secrets |
| `/opt/n8n-runner/configure-secrets.sh` | generate/persist secrets |
| `/opt/elemento/bin/healthcheck` | readiness |
| `/opt/elemento/bin/service-info` | JSON for pairing with n8n |

## Resources

Privileged Docker-in-Docker needs headroom: **4 vCPU / 8 GB RAM / ≥20 GB disk**
(see `service.yaml` prerequisites).

#!/bin/sh
# Resolve sandbox secrets into /opt/n8n-runner/runner.env (idempotent).
set -eu

ENV_FILE=/opt/n8n-runner/runner.env
SECRETS_FILE=/opt/n8n-runner/secrets.env

generate_secret() {
  if command -v openssl >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    openssl rand -hex 24
  else
    tr -dc 'a-f0-9' </dev/urandom | head -c 48
  fi
}

set_env() {
  key=$1
  value=$2
  if grep -q "^${key}=" "$ENV_FILE"; then
    sed -i.bak "s|^${key}=.*|${key}=${value}|" "$ENV_FILE"
    rm -f "${ENV_FILE}.bak"
  else
    echo "${key}=${value}" >> "$ENV_FILE"
  fi
}

is_placeholder() {
  value=$1
  [ -z "$value" ] && return 0
  echo "$value" | grep -q '{' && return 0
  echo "$value" | grep -Eq '^(change-me|CHANGEME)' && return 0
  return 1
}

if [ -f "$ENV_FILE" ]; then
  # shellcheck disable=SC1090
  . "$ENV_FILE"
fi

# Prefer previously generated secrets across restarts.
if [ -f "$SECRETS_FILE" ] && [ -s "$SECRETS_FILE" ]; then
  # shellcheck disable=SC1090
  . "$SECRETS_FILE"
fi

API_KEY="${SANDBOX_API_KEYS:-}"
REG_TOKEN="${SANDBOX_API_RUNNER_REGISTRATION_TOKEN:-}"
RUNNER_KEY="${SANDBOX_API_RUNNER_API_KEY:-}"

if is_placeholder "$API_KEY"; then
  API_KEY=$(generate_secret)
fi
if is_placeholder "$REG_TOKEN"; then
  REG_TOKEN=$(generate_secret)
fi
if is_placeholder "$RUNNER_KEY"; then
  RUNNER_KEY=$(generate_secret)
fi

umask 077
cat > "$SECRETS_FILE" <<EOF
SANDBOX_API_KEYS=${API_KEY}
SANDBOX_API_RUNNER_REGISTRATION_TOKEN=${REG_TOKEN}
SANDBOX_API_RUNNER_API_KEY=${RUNNER_KEY}
EOF
chmod 600 "$SECRETS_FILE"

set_env SANDBOX_API_KEYS "$API_KEY"
set_env SANDBOX_API_RUNNER_REGISTRATION_TOKEN "$REG_TOKEN"
set_env SANDBOX_API_RUNNER_API_KEY "$RUNNER_KEY"
chmod 600 "$ENV_FILE"

echo "n8n-runner secrets ready in $ENV_FILE" >&2

# n8n (`n8n_v3`)

Workflow automation with optional Instance AI ([`n8n_runner_v1`](../n8n_runner_v1))
and optional Qdrant peer config ([`qdrant_v1`](../qdrant_v1)).

## Pair with Qdrant

1. On the Qdrant VM:

   ```bash
   sudo /opt/elemento/bin/service-info
   # endpoints.api, credentials.tokens[0], n8n_v3_variables
   ```

2. Launch n8n with peer vars + CA trust:

   ```bash
   python -m cloudinit_manager n8n_v3 \
     -v qdrant_url=https://<qdrant-ip>.nip.io \
     -v qdrant_api_key=<token> \
     -v ca_url=http://<qdrant-or-caddy-ca>/ca.crt
   ```

3. In the n8n editor, either:
   - **HTTP Request** to `$env.QDRANT_URL/collections` with header `api-key: {{$env.QDRANT_API_KEY}}`, or
   - Create a **Qdrant / API** credential using the same URL and key.

These env vars are for discoverability — n8n does not auto-bind them into nodes.

## On-VM ops

```bash
sudo /opt/elemento/bin/healthcheck
sudo /opt/elemento/bin/service-info
```

#!/bin/sh
# Enable Instance AI only when sandbox (+ optional model) vars are real values.
set -eu

ENV_FILE=/opt/n8n/.env

is_placeholder() {
  value=$1
  [ -z "$value" ] && return 0
  echo "$value" | grep -q '{' && return 0
  return 1
}

set_env() {
  key=$1
  value=$2
  if grep -q "^${key}=" "$ENV_FILE"; then
    # Escape | in value for sed
    esc=$(printf '%s' "$value" | sed 's/[|&\\]/\\&/g')
    sed -i.bak "s|^${key}=.*|${key}=${esc}|" "$ENV_FILE"
    rm -f "${ENV_FILE}.bak"
  else
    echo "${key}=${value}" >> "$ENV_FILE"
  fi
}

[ -f "$ENV_FILE" ] || exit 0
# shellcheck disable=SC1090
. "$ENV_FILE"

SANDBOX_URL="${N8N_INSTANCE_AI_SANDBOX_API_URL:-}"
SANDBOX_KEY="${N8N_INSTANCE_AI_SANDBOX_API_KEY:-}"
# Prefer the current n8n sandbox service vars when present.
if ! is_placeholder "${N8N_SANDBOX_SERVICE_URL:-}"; then
  SANDBOX_URL="$N8N_SANDBOX_SERVICE_URL"
fi
if ! is_placeholder "${N8N_SANDBOX_SERVICE_API_KEY:-}"; then
  SANDBOX_KEY="$N8N_SANDBOX_SERVICE_API_KEY"
fi

if is_placeholder "$SANDBOX_URL" || is_placeholder "$SANDBOX_KEY"; then
  echo "Instance AI sandbox not configured; leaving AI modules disabled" >&2
  set_env N8N_ENABLED_MODULES ""
  set_env N8N_INSTANCE_AI_SANDBOX_ENABLED "false"
  set_env N8N_INSTANCE_AI_SANDBOX_API_URL ""
  set_env N8N_INSTANCE_AI_SANDBOX_API_KEY ""
  set_env N8N_SANDBOX_SERVICE_URL ""
  set_env N8N_SANDBOX_SERVICE_API_KEY ""
  set_env N8N_INSTANCE_AI_MODEL ""
  set_env N8N_INSTANCE_AI_MODEL_URL ""
  set_env N8N_INSTANCE_AI_MODEL_API_KEY ""
  exit 0
fi

modules="${N8N_ENABLED_MODULES:-}"
if is_placeholder "$modules"; then
  modules="instance-ai"
fi
set_env N8N_ENABLED_MODULES "$modules"
set_env N8N_INSTANCE_AI_SANDBOX_ENABLED "true"
set_env N8N_INSTANCE_AI_SANDBOX_PROVIDER "n8n-sandbox"
set_env N8N_INSTANCE_AI_SANDBOX_API_URL "$SANDBOX_URL"
set_env N8N_INSTANCE_AI_SANDBOX_API_KEY "$SANDBOX_KEY"
# n8n (≥ recent Instance AI) requires these for provider=n8n-sandbox.
set_env N8N_SANDBOX_SERVICE_URL "$SANDBOX_URL"
set_env N8N_SANDBOX_SERVICE_API_KEY "$SANDBOX_KEY"

model="${N8N_INSTANCE_AI_MODEL:-}"
if is_placeholder "$model"; then
  # OpenAI-compatible custom endpoint: model id is whatever the backend expects.
  model="openai/gpt-4o-mini"
fi

model_url="${N8N_INSTANCE_AI_MODEL_URL:-}"
if is_placeholder "$model_url"; then
  set_env N8N_INSTANCE_AI_MODEL_URL ""
  model_url=""
fi

# With MODEL_URL set, n8n must not treat "google/…" / "openai/…" as built-in
# providers (that yields Google/OpenAI SDK paths against an OpenAI-compatible
# base URL and 401s on Caddy). Prefer custom/<model-id>.
if [ -n "$model_url" ]; then
  case "$model" in
    custom/*) ;;
    *) model="custom/${model}" ;;
  esac
fi
set_env N8N_INSTANCE_AI_MODEL "$model"

model_key="${N8N_INSTANCE_AI_MODEL_API_KEY:-}"
if is_placeholder "$model_key"; then
  set_env N8N_INSTANCE_AI_MODEL_API_KEY ""
fi

echo "Instance AI enabled; sandbox=$SANDBOX_URL model=$model" >&2

#!/bin/sh
# Fetch an optional peer Caddy CA bundle for outbound HTTPS (NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS).
set -eu

ENV_FILE=/opt/n8n/.env
EXTRA_CA=/opt/n8n/extra-cas.pem

is_placeholder() {
  value=$1
  [ -z "$value" ] && return 0
  echo "$value" | grep -q '{' && return 0
  return 1
}

set_env() {
  key=$1
  value=$2
  if grep -q "^${key}=" "$ENV_FILE"; then
    esc=$(printf '%s' "$value" | sed 's/[|&\\]/\\&/g')
    sed -i.bak "s|^${key}=.*|${key}=${esc}|" "$ENV_FILE"
    rm -f "${ENV_FILE}.bak"
  else
    echo "${key}=${value}" >> "$ENV_FILE"
  fi
}

unset_env() {
  key=$1
  if grep -q "^${key}=" "$ENV_FILE"; then
    grep -v "^${key}=" "$ENV_FILE" > "${ENV_FILE}.tmp" || true
    mv "${ENV_FILE}.tmp" "$ENV_FILE"
  fi
}

normalize_ca_url() {
  u=$1
  [ -n "$u" ] || return 1
  echo "$u" | grep -q '{' && return 1
  case "$u" in
    http://*|https://*)
      case "$u" in
        */ca.crt|*/cas.json|*.pem|*.crt) printf '%s\n' "$u" ;;
        */) printf '%sca.crt\n' "$u" ;;
        *) printf '%s/ca.crt\n' "$u" ;;
      esac
      ;;
    *) printf 'http://%s/ca.crt\n' "$u" ;;
  esac
}

fetch_pem() {
  url=$1
  case "$url" in
    https://*) curl -fskS --max-time 10 "$url" ;;
    *) curl -fsS --max-time 10 "$url" ;;
  esac
}

[ -f "$ENV_FILE" ] || exit 0
# shellcheck disable=SC1090
. "$ENV_FILE"

touch "$EXTRA_CA"
chmod 644 "$EXTRA_CA"
unset_env NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS

ca_url="${CA_URL:-}"
if is_placeholder "$ca_url"; then
  set_env CA_URL ""
  echo "No CA_URL configured; outbound HTTPS will not trust Caddy tls-internal peers" >&2
  exit 0
fi

url=$(normalize_ca_url "$ca_url" || true)
if [ -z "$url" ]; then
  set_env CA_URL ""
  echo "WARN: CA_URL is not a usable URL: $ca_url" >&2
  exit 0
fi

pem=""
i=0
while [ "$i" -lt 6 ]; do
  if pem=$(fetch_pem "$url" 2>/dev/null) && echo "$pem" | grep -q "BEGIN CERTIFICATE"; then
    break
  fi
  pem=""
  i=$((i + 1))
  sleep 5
done

if [ -z "$pem" ]; then
  set_env CA_URL "$url"
  echo "WARN: could not fetch Caddy CA from $url" >&2
  exit 0
fi

printf '%s\n' "$pem" > "$EXTRA_CA"

#!/bin/sh
# Normalize optional Qdrant peer env for workflows ($env / credentials docs).
set -eu

ENV_FILE=/opt/n8n/.env

is_placeholder() {
  value=$1
  [ -z "$value" ] && return 0
  echo "$value" | grep -q '{' && return 0
  return 1
}

read_env() {
  env_key=$1
  grep -E "^${env_key}=" "$ENV_FILE" 2>/dev/null | tail -1 | cut -d= -f2- || true
}

set_env() {
  key=$1
  value=$2
  if grep -q "^${key}=" "$ENV_FILE"; then
    esc=$(printf '%s' "$value" | sed 's/[|&\\]/\\&/g')
    sed -i.bak "s|^${key}=.*|${key}=${esc}|" "$ENV_FILE"
    rm -f "${ENV_FILE}.bak"
  else
    echo "${key}=${value}" >> "$ENV_FILE"
  fi
}

[ -f "$ENV_FILE" ] || exit 0

qdrant_url="$(read_env QDRANT_URL)"
qdrant_key="$(read_env QDRANT_API_KEY)"
if is_placeholder "$qdrant_url"; then qdrant_url=""; fi
if is_placeholder "$qdrant_key"; then qdrant_key=""; fi

fi

set_env QDRANT_URL "$qdrant_url"
set_env QDRANT_API_KEY "$qdrant_key"

if [ -n "$qdrant_url" ] && [ -z "$qdrant_key" ]; then
  echo "WARN: QDRANT_URL is set but QDRANT_API_KEY is empty" >&2
fi

if [ -n "$qdrant_url" ]; then
  echo "Qdrant peer configured (url=${qdrant_url})" >&2

# Nginx Proxy Manager (`npm_v1`)

[Nginx Proxy Manager](https://nginxproxymanager.com/) — clicky UI to put
Elemento services behind nice FQDNs (proxy hosts, SSL, access lists).

NPM owns ports **80 / 443 / 81** (no Caddy in front). Point DNS (or
`*.nip.io` / `/etc/hosts`) at this VM, then create Proxy Hosts to peer
`service-info` URLs.

## Launch

```bash
python -m cloudinit_manager npm_v1
```

On the VM:

```bash
sudo /opt/elemento/bin/healthcheck
sudo /opt/elemento/bin/service-info
```

1. Open `endpoints.admin` (`http://<ip>:81`)
2. Sign in with the first-boot defaults from `credentials` (then change them)
3. **Hosts → Proxy Hosts → Add**  
   - Domain: e.g. `n8n.lab` or `n8n.<npm-ip>.nip.io`  
   - Forward hostname/port: peer from that service’s `service-info`  
   - Scheme: `https` when the peer uses Caddy `tls internal`  
   - Enable Websockets if needed (n8n, Open WebUI, …)
4. SSL: Let’s Encrypt when the FQDN is publicly reachable; otherwise upload /
   use a custom cert, or terminate HTTP-only on the LAN

## Upstream TLS (`tls internal`)

Peers like `n8n_v3` / `minio_v1` present Caddy internal certs. In the proxy
host, turn on **“SSL” → “Force SSL”** only if NPM has a cert for the *public*
name. For the upstream hop, enable **“Forward scheme: https”** and consider
disabling certificate verification for private CAs, or install the peer /
[`caddy_ca_v1`](../caddy_ca_v1) bundle on the NPM host.

## Variables

None required. Optional env in `npm.env`:

| Variable | Purpose | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `DISABLE_IPV6` | Passed through to NPM | `true` |

## Notes

- Image: `jc21/nginx-proxy-manager:2.12.3` (pinned).
- Data: `/var/lib/npm/data`, certs: `/var/lib/npm/letsencrypt`.
- First-boot login: `admin@example.com` / `changeme` (NPM default).

#!/bin/sh
set -eu

ENV_FILE=/opt/openclaw/openclaw.env
CADDYFILE=/opt/openclaw/Caddyfile

if [ -f "$ENV_FILE" ]; then
  # shellcheck disable=SC1090
  . "$ENV_FILE"
fi

if [ "${OPENCLAW_ENABLE_CADDY:-false}" != "true" ]; then
  exit 0
fi

PORT="${OPENCLAW_GATEWAY_PORT:-18789}"
UPSTREAM="127.0.0.1"

meta() {
  curl -fsS --max-time 2 -H "Metadata-Flavor: Google" \
    "http://metadata.google.internal/computeMetadata/v1/$1" 2>/dev/null || true
}

add_ip() {
  ip=$1
  [ -n "$ip" ] || return 0
  echo "$ip" | grep -Eq '^[0-9]{1,3}(\.[0-9]{1,3}){3}$' || return 0
  case "$ip" in
    127.*) return 0 ;;
  esac
  echo "$ip"
}

is_private() {
  case "$1" in
    10.*|192.168.*|172.1[6-9].*|172.2[0-9].*|172.3[0-1].*) return 0 ;;
    *) return 1 ;;
  esac
}

ips=$(
  {
    hostname -I | tr ' ' '\n'
    meta instance/network-interfaces/ | tr '/' '\n' | grep -E '^[0-9]+$' | while read -r nic; do
      add_ip "$(meta "instance/network-interfaces/${nic}/ip")"
      meta "instance/network-interfaces/${nic}/access-configs/" | tr '/' '\n' | grep -E '^[0-9]+$' | while read -r ac; do
        add_ip "$(meta "instance/network-interfaces/${nic}/access-configs/${ac}/external-ip")"
      done
    done
  } | while read -r ip; do
    add_ip "$ip"
  done | sort -u
)

addrs=":443"
public_domain=""
private_domain=""
origins=""
for ip in $ips; do
  domain="${ip}.nip.io"
  addrs="${addrs}, ${domain}"
  if [ -n "$origins" ]; then
    origins="${origins},"
  fi
  origins="${origins}https://${domain},wss://${domain}"
  if is_private "$ip"; then
    [ -n "$private_domain" ] || private_domain="$domain"
  else
    [ -n "$public_domain" ] || public_domain="$domain"
  fi
done
primary="${public_domain:-$private_domain}"

# Match the proven openclaw.sh proxy: force HTTP/1.1 + Connection Upgrade for WSS.
# :80 exports the tls-internal root CA so private-IP peers can trust this instance.
# auto_https disable_redirects keeps http://<ip>/ca.crt from 308'ing to HTTPS.
cat > "$CADDYFILE" <<EOF
{
  auto_https disable_redirects
}

:80 {
    handle /ca.crt {
        root * /data/caddy/pki/authorities/local
        rewrite * /root.crt
        header Content-Type application/x-pem-file
        file_server
    }
    handle {
        respond "Elemento Caddy CA export. GET /ca.crt" 200
    }
}

${addrs} {
    tls internal
    reverse_proxy ${UPSTREAM}:${PORT} {
        header_up Host {host}
        header_up X-Forwarded-For {remote_host}
        header_up X-Real-IP {remote_host}
        header_up X-Forwarded-Proto {scheme}
        header_up Connection "Upgrade"
        transport http {
            versions 1.1
            keepalive 30s
        }
    }
}
EOF

set_env() {
  key=$1
  value=$2
  if grep -q "^${key}=" "$ENV_FILE"; then
    sed -i "s|^${key}=.*|${key}=${value}|" "$ENV_FILE"
  else
    echo "${key}=${value}" >> "$ENV_FILE"
  fi
}

if [ -n "$primary" ]; then
  set_env OPENCLAW_CADDY_DOMAIN "$primary"

#!/bin/sh
# Run on the VM, e.g.: multipass exec <vm> -- /opt/openclaw/healthcheck.sh
set -eu

ENV_FILE=/opt/openclaw/openclaw.env

fail() {
  echo "FAIL: $*" >&2
  exit 1
}

ok() {
  echo "OK: $*"
}

if [ -f "$ENV_FILE" ]; then
  # shellcheck disable=SC1090
  . "$ENV_FILE"
fi

PORT="${OPENCLAW_GATEWAY_PORT:-18789}"
ENABLE_CADDY="${OPENCLAW_ENABLE_CADDY:-false}"

pick_lan_ip() {
  for ip in $(hostname -I); do
    case "$ip" in
      *:*|127.*|172.17.*) continue ;;
    esac
    case "$ip" in
      10.*|192.168.*|172.1[6-9].*|172.2[0-9].*|172.3[0-1].*)
        echo "$ip"
        return 0
        ;;
    esac
  done
  for ip in $(hostname -I); do
    case "$ip" in
      *:*|127.*) continue ;;
      *.*.*.*)
        echo "$ip"
        return 0
        ;;
    esac
  done
  echo "127.0.0.1"
}

command -v curl >/dev/null 2>&1 || fail "curl not installed"
command -v systemctl >/dev/null 2>&1 || fail "systemctl not available"

[ -f /usr/lib/node_modules/openclaw/dist/index.js ] || fail "openclaw install missing"
[ -f /root/.openclaw/openclaw.json ] || fail "openclaw.json missing"

systemctl is-active --quiet openclaw-gateway.service || fail "openclaw-gateway.service is not active"

code=$(curl -sS -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}" --max-time 5 \
  "http://127.0.0.1:${PORT}/" || true)
case "$code" in
  2??|3??|4??) ok "OpenClaw gateway responded with $code on :${PORT}" ;;
  *) fail "OpenClaw gateway check failed (status=${code:-unreachable})" ;;
esac

if [ "$ENABLE_CADDY" = "true" ]; then
  command -v docker >/dev/null 2>&1 || fail "docker not installed (required when Caddy is enabled)"
  docker info >/dev/null 2>&1 || fail "docker daemon not reachable"
  docker compose -f /opt/openclaw/docker-compose.caddy.yml ps --status running --format '{{.Service}}' 2>/dev/null \
    | grep -qx caddy || fail "caddy compose service is not running"

  # Probe a hostname on the tls-internal cert (not https://127.0.0.1 — SNI mismatch).
  domain="${OPENCLAW_CADDY_DOMAIN:-}"
  if [ -z "$domain" ] || echo "$domain" | grep -q ':' ; then
    domain="$(pick_lan_ip).nip.io"
  fi
  caddy_code=$(curl -skS -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}" --max-time 5 "https://${domain}/" || true)
  case "$caddy_code" in
    2??|3??|4??) ok "Caddy HTTPS responded with $caddy_code on https://${domain}/" ;;
    *) fail "Caddy HTTPS check failed for https://${domain}/ (status=${caddy_code:-unreachable})" ;;
  esac

  pem=$(curl -fsS --max-time 5 "http://127.0.0.1/ca.crt" || true)
  echo "$pem" | grep -q "BEGIN CERTIFICATE" || fail "Caddy CA export missing at http://127.0.0.1/ca.crt"
  ok "Caddy CA exported on http://127.0.0.1/ca.crt"
fi

# Open WebUI (`openwebui_v1`)

Model-agnostic chat WebUI based on [Open WebUI](https://github.com/open-webui/open-webui).
Talks to any **OpenAI-compatible** HTTP API — including [`llmstudio_v1`](../llmstudio_v1),
OpenAI, OpenRouter, Groq, vLLM, and similar — and optionally Ollama.
Optional Knowledge / RAG via [`qdrant_v1`](../qdrant_v1).

## Pair with LM Studio

1. Launch `llmstudio_v1` and read tokens / URL:

   ```bash
   sudo /opt/elemento/bin/service-info   # on the LM Studio VM
   ```

2. Launch Open WebUI pointing at that API:

   ```bash
   python -m cloudinit_manager openwebui_v1 \
     -v openai_base_url=https://<llmstudio-host>/v1 \
     -v openai_api_key=<bearer-from-service-info> \
     -v ca_url=http://<llmstudio-ip>/ca.crt
   ```

3. Open `https://<openwebui-ip>.nip.io/` (Caddy uses an internal TLS CA).

## Pair with Qdrant (Knowledge / RAG)

1. Launch `qdrant_v1` and read connection info:

   ```bash
   sudo /opt/elemento/bin/service-info   # on the Qdrant VM
   # endpoints.api + credentials.tokens[0]
   ```

2. Launch (or re-render) Open WebUI with Qdrant + an embedding-capable LLM:

   ```bash
   python -m cloudinit_manager openwebui_v1 \
     -v openai_base_url=https://<llmstudio-host>/v1 \
     -v openai_api_key=<lms-token> \
     -v qdrant_uri=https://<qdrant-ip>.nip.io \
     -v qdrant_api_key=<qdrant-token> \
     -v ca_url=http://<caddy-ca-or-peer>/ca.crt
   ```

Use official Open WebUI env **`QDRANT_URI`** (HTTPS base from `endpoints.api`; no
`:6333`, no path). When `qdrant_uri` is set, configure sets `VECTOR_DB=qdrant`.

If LM Studio and Qdrant use different Caddy roots, point `ca_url` at
[`caddy_ca_v1`](../caddy_ca_v1) with both peers.

Switching from default Chroma to Qdrant does not migrate existing embeddings;
re-ingest Knowledge after the change.

## Other providers

```bash
# OpenAI
python -m cloudinit_manager openwebui_v1 \
  -v openai_base_url=https://api.openai.com/v1 \
  -v openai_api_key=sk-...

# Several OpenAI-compatible backends (semicolon-separated)
python -m cloudinit_manager openwebui_v1 \
  -v openai_base_urls='https://host-a/v1;https://host-b/v1' \
  -v openai_api_keys='token-a;token-b'

# Ollama on another host
python -m cloudinit_manager openwebui_v1 \
  -v enable_ollama_api=true \
  -v ollama_base_url=http://<ollama-host>:11434
```

Leave `openai_base_url` unset to configure providers later in the Open WebUI admin UI.

## Variables

| Variable | Purpose | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `openai_base_url` | Single OpenAI-compatible base (`…/v1`) | empty |
| `openai_api_key` | Bearer / API key for that base | empty |
| `openai_base_urls` / `openai_api_keys` | Multi-provider (`;`-separated) | empty |
| `qdrant_uri` | Qdrant HTTPS base (`qdrant_v1` `endpoints.api`) | empty |
| `qdrant_api_key` | Qdrant API key (`api-key` header) | empty |
| `vector_db` | Open WebUI vector backend | `qdrant` when URI set; else empty (Chroma) |
| `webui_auth` | Require signup/login | `true` |
| `webui_secret_key` | Session secret (generated if unset) | generated |
| `enable_ollama_api` / `ollama_base_url` | Optional Ollama client | off / empty |
| `ca_url` | Peer Caddy CA (`http://<ip>/ca.crt` or [`caddy_ca_v1`](../caddy_ca_v1)) | empty |

## On-VM ops

```bash
sudo /opt/elemento/bin/healthcheck
sudo /opt/elemento/bin/service-info
docker compose -f /opt/openwebui/docker-compose.yml logs -f openwebui
```

## Notes

- HTTPS uses Caddy `tls internal` (same pattern as `n8n_v3` / `llmstudio_v1`).
- Port 80 exports `GET /ca.crt` (the local Caddy root) for private-IP peers.
- Set `ca_url` so Open WebUI trusts other Elemento Caddy backends instead of
  disabling TLS verification. Without it, `AIOHTTP_CLIENT_SESSION_SSL=false`.
- Image: `ghcr.io/open-webui/open-webui:main` (unpinned; pin a tag for production reproducibility).
