#!/bin/sh
# Normalize Open WebUI env: secrets, placeholders, OpenAI-compatible backends.
set -eu

ENV_FILE=/opt/openwebui/openwebui.env
CADDYFILE=/opt/openwebui/Caddyfile

is_placeholder() {
  _value=$1
  [ -z "$_value" ] && return 0
  echo "$_value" | grep -q '{' && return 0
  return 1
}

read_env() {
  # Use env_key — never "key" — so we do not clobber the caller's api_key.
  env_key=$1
  grep -E "^${env_key}=" "$ENV_FILE" 2>/dev/null | tail -1 | cut -d= -f2- || true
}

generate_secret() {
  if command -v openssl >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    openssl rand -hex 32
  else
    tr -dc 'a-f0-9' </dev/urandom | head -c 64
  fi
}

set_env() {
  # Use env_key/env_val — never "key" — so we do not clobber the caller's api_key.
  env_key=$1
  env_val=$2
  if grep -q "^${env_key}=" "$ENV_FILE"; then
    esc=$(printf '%s' "$env_val" | sed 's/[|&\\]/\\&/g')
    sed -i.bak "s|^${env_key}=.*|${env_key}=${esc}|" "$ENV_FILE"
    rm -f "${ENV_FILE}.bak"
  else
    echo "${env_key}=${env_val}" >> "$ENV_FILE"
  fi
}

unset_env() {
  env_key=$1
  if grep -q "^${env_key}=" "$ENV_FILE"; then
    grep -v "^${env_key}=" "$ENV_FILE" > "${ENV_FILE}.tmp" || true
    mv "${ENV_FILE}.tmp" "$ENV_FILE"
  fi
}

normalize_ca_url() {
  u=$1
  [ -n "$u" ] || return 1
  echo "$u" | grep -q '{' && return 1
  case "$u" in
    http://*|https://*)
      case "$u" in
        */ca.crt|*/cas.json|*.pem|*.crt) printf '%s\n' "$u" ;;
        */) printf '%sca.crt\n' "$u" ;;
        *) printf '%s/ca.crt\n' "$u" ;;
      esac
      ;;
    *) printf 'http://%s/ca.crt\n' "$u" ;;
  esac
}

fetch_pem() {
  url=$1
  case "$url" in
    https://*) curl -fskS --max-time 10 "$url" ;;
    *) curl -fsS --max-time 10 "$url" ;;
  esac
}

install_peer_ca() {
  ca_url=$1
  bundle=/opt/openwebui/ca-bundle.pem
  extra=/opt/openwebui/extra-cas.pem
  : > "$bundle"
  unset_env SSL_CERT_FILE
  unset_env REQUESTS_CA_BUNDLE
  set_env AIOHTTP_CLIENT_SESSION_SSL "false"
  if is_placeholder "$ca_url"; then
    set_env CA_URL ""
    return 0
  fi
  url=$(normalize_ca_url "$ca_url" || true)
  if [ -z "$url" ]; then
    set_env CA_URL ""
    return 0
  fi
  pem=""
  i=0
  while [ "$i" -lt 6 ]; do
    if pem=$(fetch_pem "$url" 2>/dev/null) && echo "$pem" | grep -q "BEGIN CERTIFICATE"; then
      break
    fi
    pem=""
    i=$((i + 1))
    sleep 5
  done
  if [ -z "$pem" ]; then
    set_env CA_URL "$url"
    echo "WARN: could not fetch Caddy CA from $url" >&2
    return 0
  fi
  printf '%s\n' "$pem" > "$extra"
  if [ -f /etc/ssl/certs/ca-certificates.crt ]; then
    cat /etc/ssl/certs/ca-certificates.crt "$extra" > "$bundle"
  else
    cp "$extra" "$bundle"
  fi
  chmod 644 "$bundle"
  set_env CA_URL "$url"
  set_env SSL_CERT_FILE "/etc/ssl/openwebui-ca-bundle.pem"
  set_env REQUESTS_CA_BUNDLE "/etc/ssl/openwebui-ca-bundle.pem"
  set_env AIOHTTP_CLIENT_SESSION_SSL "true"
  echo "Installed peer Caddy CA from $url" >&2
}

pick_lan_ip() {
  for ip in $(hostname -I); do
    case "$ip" in
      *:*|127.*|172.17.*) continue ;;
    esac
    case "$ip" in
      10.*|192.168.*|172.1[6-9].*|172.2[0-9].*|172.3[0-1].*)
        echo "$ip"
        return 0
        ;;
    esac
  done
  for ip in $(hostname -I); do
    case "$ip" in
      *:*|127.*) continue ;;
      *.*.*.*)
        echo "$ip"
        return 0
        ;;
    esac
  done
  echo "127.0.0.1"
}

[ -f "$ENV_FILE" ] || exit 0

secret="$(read_env WEBUI_SECRET_KEY)"
if is_placeholder "$secret"; then
  secret=$(generate_secret)
fi
set_env WEBUI_SECRET_KEY "$secret"

auth="$(read_env WEBUI_AUTH)"
if is_placeholder "$auth"; then
  auth="true"
fi
set_env WEBUI_AUTH "$auth"

base="$(read_env OPENAI_API_BASE_URL)"
api_key="$(read_env OPENAI_API_KEY)"
bases="$(read_env OPENAI_API_BASE_URLS)"
api_keys="$(read_env OPENAI_API_KEYS)"

if is_placeholder "$bases"; then bases=""; fi
if is_placeholder "$api_keys"; then api_keys=""; fi
if is_placeholder "$base"; then base=""; fi
if is_placeholder "$api_key"; then api_key=""; fi

# Prefer multi-provider lists when provided; otherwise single base/key.
if [ -n "$bases" ]; then
  set_env OPENAI_API_BASE_URLS "$bases"
  set_env OPENAI_API_KEYS "${api_keys:-$api_key}"
  set_env OPENAI_API_BASE_URL ""
  set_env OPENAI_API_KEY ""
else
  set_env OPENAI_API_BASE_URLS ""
  set_env OPENAI_API_KEYS ""
  set_env OPENAI_API_BASE_URL "$base"
  set_env OPENAI_API_KEY "$api_key"
fi

ollama_enabled="$(read_env ENABLE_OLLAMA_API)"
ollama_url="$(read_env OLLAMA_BASE_URL)"
if is_placeholder "$ollama_url"; then ollama_url=""; fi
if is_placeholder "$ollama_enabled"; then
  if [ -n "$ollama_url" ]; then
    ollama_enabled="true"
  else
    ollama_enabled="false"
  fi
fi
set_env ENABLE_OLLAMA_API "$ollama_enabled"
set_env OLLAMA_BASE_URL "$ollama_url"
set_env ENABLE_OPENAI_API "true"

# Optional Qdrant vector store (Knowledge / RAG). Official env is QDRANT_URI.
qdrant_uri="$(read_env QDRANT_URI)"
qdrant_key="$(read_env QDRANT_API_KEY)"
vector_db="$(read_env VECTOR_DB)"
if is_placeholder "$qdrant_uri"; then qdrant_uri=""; fi
if is_placeholder "$qdrant_key"; then qdrant_key=""; fi
if is_placeholder "$vector_db"; then vector_db=""; fi
if [ -n "$qdrant_uri" ]; then
  qdrant_uri=$(printf '%s' "$qdrant_uri" | sed 's|/*$||')
  if [ -z "$vector_db" ]; then
    vector_db="qdrant"
  fi
fi
set_env QDRANT_URI "$qdrant_uri"
set_env QDRANT_API_KEY "$qdrant_key"
set_env VECTOR_DB "$vector_db"
# qdrant_v1 does not expose gRPC on the host.
unset_env QDRANT_PREFER_GRPC
unset_env QDRANT_GRPC_PORT

# Env vars must win over Admin UI / DB on appliance boots (see Open WebUI docs).
set_env ENABLE_PERSISTENT_CONFIG "false"
# LM Studio and other Caddy-fronted backends often use internal TLS.
# When CA_URL is set and fetched, we install the PEM and re-enable verification.
install_peer_ca "$(read_env CA_URL)"

# Resolve __OPENWEBUI_DOMAIN__ / hostname -I docker-bridge / IPv6 mistakes.
domain="$(read_env WEBUI_HOST)"
if [ -z "$domain" ] || echo "$domain" | grep -q '__OPENWEBUI_DOMAIN__\|{\|:'; then
  domain="$(pick_lan_ip).nip.io"
fi
set_env WEBUI_HOST "$domain"
set_env WEBUI_URL "https://${domain}"

# Idempotent: rewrite HTTPS site address even after __OPENWEBUI_DOMAIN__ was replaced.
if [ -f "$CADDYFILE" ]; then
  awk -v domain="$domain" '
    BEGIN { done = 0 }
    /^[[:space:]]*#/ { print; next }
    /^:80([[:space:]]|\{)/ { print; next }
    /^\{/ { print; next }
    !done && /^[^#[:space:]].*\{/ {
      print domain " {"
      done = 1
      next
    }
    { print }
  ' "$CADDYFILE" > "${CADDYFILE}.tmp"
  mv "${CADDYFILE}.tmp" "$CADDYFILE"
fi

# Drop any unreplaced template placeholders so docker env_file stays clean.
grep -v '{{' "$ENV_FILE" > "${ENV_FILE}.tmp" || true
mv "${ENV_FILE}.tmp" "$ENV_FILE"
chmod 600 "$ENV_FILE"

if [ -n "$base" ] && [ -z "$api_key" ] && [ -z "$api_keys" ]; then
  echo "WARN: OPENAI_API_BASE_URL is set but OPENAI_API_KEY is empty" >&2
fi

if [ -n "$qdrant_uri" ] && [ -z "$qdrant_key" ]; then
  echo "WARN: QDRANT_URI is set but QDRANT_API_KEY is empty" >&2
fi

echo "Open WebUI env ready (domain=${domain} openai_base=${base:-none} ollama=${ollama_enabled} qdrant=${qdrant_uri:-none})" >&2

#!/bin/sh
# Normalize Postgres env: mint password when placeholder/empty.
set -eu

ENV_FILE=/opt/postgres/postgres.env

is_placeholder() {
  _value=$1
  [ -z "$_value" ] && return 0
  echo "$_value" | grep -q '{' && return 0
  return 1
}

read_env() {
  env_key=$1
  grep -E "^${env_key}=" "$ENV_FILE" 2>/dev/null | tail -1 | cut -d= -f2- || true
}

generate_secret() {
  if command -v openssl >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    openssl rand -hex 32
  else
    tr -dc 'a-f0-9' </dev/urandom | head -c 64
  fi
}

set_env() {
  env_key=$1
  env_val=$2
  if grep -q "^${env_key}=" "$ENV_FILE"; then
    esc=$(printf '%s' "$env_val" | sed 's/[|&\\]/\\&/g')
    sed -i.bak "s|^${env_key}=.*|${env_key}=${esc}|" "$ENV_FILE"
    rm -f "${ENV_FILE}.bak"
  else
    echo "${env_key}=${env_val}" >> "$ENV_FILE"
  fi
}

[ -f "$ENV_FILE" ] || exit 0

password="$(read_env POSTGRES_PASSWORD)"
if is_placeholder "$password"; then
  password=$(generate_secret)
fi
set_env POSTGRES_PASSWORD "$password"

user="$(read_env POSTGRES_USER)"
if is_placeholder "$user"; then
  user=elemento
fi
set_env POSTGRES_USER "$user"

db="$(read_env POSTGRES_DB)"
if is_placeholder "$db"; then
  db=elemento
fi
set_env POSTGRES_DB "$db"

grep -v '{{' "$ENV_FILE" > "${ENV_FILE}.tmp" || true
mv "${ENV_FILE}.tmp" "$ENV_FILE"
chmod 600 "$ENV_FILE"

echo "Postgres env ready (user=${user} db=${db})" >&2

# Qdrant (`qdrant_v1`)

[Qdrant](https://qdrant.tech/) vector database with HTTPS via Caddy (`tls internal`)
and the **built-in Web UI** (collections, points, console, access tokens).

## Web UI

```bash
sudo /opt/elemento/bin/service-info   # on the Qdrant VM
```

1. Open `https://<ip>.nip.io/` (redirects to `/dashboard`) or
   `https://<ip>.nip.io/dashboard`
2. Accept the self-signed / internal TLS warning in the browser
3. Paste the API key from `credentials.tokens[0]` when the UI prompts

Pair with [`dify_v1`](../dify_v1) only if you want Dify knowledge-base ingest on top;
the Qdrant UI alone is enough to browse and manage collections.

## Pair with Open WebUI or n8n

`service-info` includes copy-paste peer maps:

- `openwebui_v1_variables` → `-v qdrant_uri=… -v qdrant_api_key=…`
- `n8n_v3_variables` → `-v qdrant_url=… -v qdrant_api_key=…`

Also pass `ca_url=http://<qdrant-ip>/ca.crt` (or [`caddy_ca_v1`](../caddy_ca_v1)).
See [`openwebui_v1`](../openwebui_v1) and [`n8n_v3`](../n8n_v3) READMEs.

## Launch

```bash
python -m cloudinit_manager qdrant_v1
# optional: -v api_key=my-secret
```

On the VM:

```bash
sudo /opt/elemento/bin/healthcheck
sudo /opt/elemento/bin/service-info
```

- UI: `https://<ip>.nip.io/dashboard`
- REST: `https://<ip>.nip.io` (header `api-key: …`)
- Peer CA: `http://<ip>/ca.crt`

## Variables

| Variable | Purpose | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `api_key` | Qdrant API key (REST + Web UI login) | generated on first boot |

## Notes

- Image: `qdrant/qdrant:v1.13.2` (pinned); Web UI is served by the same process.
- Data: `/var/lib/qdrant`.
- Only REST (6333) is published via Caddy; gRPC is not exposed on the host.

[SearXNG](https://docs.searxng.org/) metasearch with HTTPS via Caddy
(`tls internal`). Useful as a web-search backend for agents and n8n.

No application login — treat the Elemento network / firewall as the boundary.

```bash
python -m cloudinit_manager searxng_v1
# optional: -v secret=my-secret-key
```

On the VM:

```bash
sudo /opt/elemento/bin/healthcheck
sudo /opt/elemento/bin/service-info
```

- UI: `https://<ip>.nip.io/`
- JSON API: `https://<ip>.nip.io/search?q=…&format=json`
- Peer CA: `http://<ip>/ca.crt`

## Variables

| Variable | Purpose | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `secret` | SearXNG `server.secret_key` | generated on first boot |

## Notes

- Image: `searxng/searxng:2025.7.24-84c3a83` (pinned).
- Config: `/opt/searxng/settings.yml` (JSON + HTML formats enabled; limiter off).
- Cache: `/var/lib/searxng`.

#!/bin/sh
# Normalize SearXNG env + settings.yml: secret, base_url, Caddy domain.
set -eu

ENV_FILE=/opt/searxng/searxng.env
SETTINGS=/opt/searxng/settings.yml
CADDYFILE=/opt/searxng/Caddyfile

is_placeholder() {
  _value=$1
  [ -z "$_value" ] && return 0
  echo "$_value" | grep -q '{' && return 0
  return 1
}

read_env() {
  env_key=$1
  grep -E "^${env_key}=" "$ENV_FILE" 2>/dev/null | tail -1 | cut -d= -f2- || true
}

generate_secret() {
  if command -v openssl >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    openssl rand -hex 32
  else
    tr -dc 'a-f0-9' </dev/urandom | head -c 64
  fi
}

set_env() {
  env_key=$1
  env_val=$2
  if grep -q "^${env_key}=" "$ENV_FILE"; then
    esc=$(printf '%s' "$env_val" | sed 's/[|&\\]/\\&/g')
    sed -i.bak "s|^${env_key}=.*|${env_key}=${esc}|" "$ENV_FILE"
    rm -f "${ENV_FILE}.bak"
  else
    echo "${env_key}=${env_val}" >> "$ENV_FILE"
  fi
}

pick_lan_ip() {
  for ip in $(hostname -I); do
    case "$ip" in
      *:*|127.*|172.17.*) continue ;;
    esac
    case "$ip" in
      10.*|192.168.*|172.1[6-9].*|172.2[0-9].*|172.3[0-1].*)
        echo "$ip"
        return 0
        ;;
    esac
  done
  for ip in $(hostname -I); do
    case "$ip" in
      *:*|127.*) continue ;;
      *.*.*.*)
        echo "$ip"
        return 0
        ;;
    esac
  done
  echo "127.0.0.1"
}

[ -f "$ENV_FILE" ] || exit 0

secret="$(read_env SEARXNG_SECRET)"
if is_placeholder "$secret"; then
  secret=$(generate_secret)
fi
set_env SEARXNG_SECRET "$secret"

domain="$(read_env SEARXNG_HOST)"
if [ -z "$domain" ] || echo "$domain" | grep -q '__SEARXNG_DOMAIN__\|{\|:'; then
  domain="$(pick_lan_ip).nip.io"
fi
set_env SEARXNG_HOST "$domain"
set_env SEARXNG_BASE_URL "https://${domain}/"

if [ -f "$SETTINGS" ]; then
  sed -i.bak \
    -e "s|__SEARXNG_SECRET__|${secret}|g" \
    -e "s|__SEARXNG_DOMAIN__|${domain}|g" \
    "$SETTINGS"
  rm -f "${SETTINGS}.bak"
fi

if [ -f "$CADDYFILE" ]; then
  awk -v domain="$domain" '
    BEGIN { done = 0 }
    /^[[:space:]]*#/ { print; next }
    /^:80([[:space:]]|\{)/ { print; next }
    /^\{/ { print; next }
    !done && /^[^#[:space:]].*\{/ {
      print domain " {"
      done = 1
      next
    }
    { print }
  ' "$CADDYFILE" > "${CADDYFILE}.tmp"
  mv "${CADDYFILE}.tmp" "$CADDYFILE"
fi

grep -v '{{' "$ENV_FILE" > "${ENV_FILE}.tmp" || true
mv "${ENV_FILE}.tmp" "$ENV_FILE"
chmod 600 "$ENV_FILE"

echo "SearXNG env ready (domain=${domain})" >&2

      10.*|192.168.*|172.1[6-9].*|172.2[0-9].*|172.3[0-1].*)
        echo "$ip"
        return 0
        ;;
    esac
  done
  for ip in $(hostname -I); do
    case "$ip" in
      *:*|127.*) continue ;;
      *.*.*.*)
        echo "$ip"
        return 0
        ;;
    esac
  done
  echo "127.0.0.1"
}

password="${VALKEY_PASSWORD:-}"
[ -n "$password" ] || fail "VALKEY_PASSWORD missing (run configure-valkey.sh)"
echo "$password" | grep -q '{' && fail "VALKEY_PASSWORD still a placeholder"

lan_ip="$(pick_lan_ip)"
# Redis URI scheme for broad client compatibility (Valkey speaks the Redis protocol).
uri="redis://:${password}@${lan_ip}:6379/0"

cat <<EOF
{
  "api_version": "elemento.service_info/v1",
  "service": "valkey_v1",
  "status": "ready",
  "endpoints": {
    "host": "$(json_escape "$lan_ip")",
    "port": 6379,
    "local_host": "127.0.0.1",
    "local_port": 6379
  },
  "credentials": {
    "type": "password",
    "password": "$(json_escape "$password")",
    "uri": "$(json_escape "$uri")"
  }
}
EOF
